figures.intendedInference: With minPts=4 including self, counts are D=5, E=2, and F=1. Only the core neighborhood can expand.

figures.visualPremise: Locate the first failing rank and step before blaming later symptoms
figures.intendedInference: The first nonfinite value appears at rank 1, step 2. The later failures across all ranks do not identify their original cause.

figures.visualPremise: A gradient can exist while the intended parameters stay unchanged
figures.intendedInference: The same tiny batch has nonzero gradient but zero weight change. Diagnose the update path before full-data generalization.

figures.visualPremise: Assigned users still count when the treatment falls back
figures.intendedInference: This illustrative cell assigns 100 users but serves the new model to only 60. Dropping 40 fallback users changes the estimand and can bias the comparison.

figures.visualPremise: Clearing gradients does not restore training mode
figures.intendedInference: A training iteration needs both the intended model mode and a clean gradient buffer. Each action changes a separate persistent state.

figures.visualPremise: The alternative portfolio is the opportunity cost
figures.intendedInference: In this illustrative fixed-capacity choice, A yields 8 while compatible B and C yield 11. Past effort on A does not change the forward comparison.

figures.visualPremise: The second split affects only one root branch
figures.intendedInference: The root sends every x<=0 point to A. Splitting y on the right branch changes only the x>0 region.

figures.visualPremise: Do not let later luck rewrite what was known at decision time
figures.intendedInference: The original choice used the evidence available before its boundary. A favorable later outcome does not prove that the original process was sound.

figures.visualPremise: Missing outcomes are not negative outcomes
figures.intendedInference: Only observed mature outcomes supply this label. Pending, censored, and unobserved cases retain their distinct missingness states.

figures.visualPremise: A matched control separates the component from the extra resources
figures.intendedInference: The baseline scores 80; the resource-matched control scores 82.8; the claimed method scores 83. The isolated matched gap is 0.2 points, not 3.

figures.visualPremise: Shared context does not imply shared execution authority
figures.intendedInference: Inline, chat, and review can share repository context. Only an authorized isolated agent may use the declared edit and execution tools.

figures.visualPremise: Persist authority before dispatch; reconcile a lost reply
figures.intendedInference: The payment commits once under an idempotency key. A lost reply requires reconciliation, not a second payment.

figures.visualPremise: Matching model weights alone is not a consistent restart
figures.intendedInference: Rank 1 has the right model version but stale optimizer state. Recovery waits until model, optimizer, and data position agree.

figures.visualPremise: Historical lookup needs availability time as well as event time
figures.intendedInference: Version B has an 11:50 event time but arrives at 12:10. The noon lookup must return available version A, not B.

figures.visualPremise: Deleting source membership does not prove deletion of model influence
figures.intendedInference: A new shard can exclude source D7. Existing checkpoint and model influence require their own intervention and validation.

figures.visualPremise: The policy changes which payment outcomes become observable
figures.intendedInference: A declined payment has no observed repayment outcome. Pending and declined cases cannot be silently labeled as legitimate negatives.

figures.visualPremise: Fixing one reproduced attack leaves other paths unknown
figures.intendedInference: The direct request is now blocked. Quoted and tool-output paths remain untested, not passed.

figures.visualPremise: Significance, practical value, and safety are separate conditions
figures.intendedInference: One candidate has too little practical gain; another fails safety. Neither passes all launch gates.

figures.visualPremise: A freshness violation can be known before quality labels mature
figures.intendedInference: A stale snapshot breaches its current contract immediately. Quality inference still waits for mature outcomes and valid joins.

figures.visualPremise: Only the first valid compare-and-swap owns the result
figures.intendedInference: A commits version 0 to 1. B still expects version 0, so its later write is rejected rather than overwriting A.

figures.visualPremise: A successful task can still fail the authorization requirement
figures.intendedInference: Completion and policy compliance are independent checks. Unauthorized account access vetoes the otherwise successful trial.

figures.visualPremise: Persistent pages and refreshing work slots are different ledgers
figures.intendedInference: A and B reserve nine of twelve KV pages. The eight token-work slots refresh each iteration; free slots do not erase persistent page reservations.

figures.visualPremise: Quarterly hours do not describe the nodes free right now
figures.intendedInference: Six serving nodes and two offline nodes fill this instantaneous eight-node pool. Serving pressure reclaims the two offline nodes; protected reserves remain protected.

figures.visualPremise: Treatment can change supply that later reaches control
figures.intendedInference: Both cells share one creator pool. Changed supply can return to both cells, breaking a simple no-interference interpretation.

figures.visualPremise: A lower-scoring shelf can improve the whole page
figures.intendedInference: Shelf scores are A=6, B=5, C=4. A+B repeats a song and pays penalty 4; A+C wins at 10.

figures.visualPremise: Only displayed candidates have exposure-linked feedback
figures.intendedInference: Of 900 eligible candidates, only ten are displayed. The other 890 are unshown, not negative response observations.

figures.visualPremise: Reranking cannot recover a passage removed upstream
figures.intendedInference: Both required evidence passages must survive retrieval and filtering. A relevant passage dropped before reranking cannot appear in the final answer context.

figures.visualPremise: Reuse source memory while the generated prefix grows
figures.intendedInference: The encoder source key/value memory stays fixed. Decoder prefixes and their own caches grow across generation steps.

figures.visualPremise: Passing tests does not establish sustained user value
figures.intendedInference: A test receipt establishes only its tested contract. Acceptance, continued use, and durable value require separate observations.

figures.visualPremise: A passed test and an unauthorized write can coexist
figures.intendedInference: One trial can complete its task while violating the authority boundary. The combined result must fail the declared policy gate.

figures.visualPremise: A better weighted average can conceal a failing tail
figures.intendedInference: At head/tail weights 90%/10%, B averages 0.88 versus A at 0.80. Its tail score 0.70 misses the 0.78 floor.

figures.visualPremise: A benchmark becomes development evidence when it guides selection
figures.intendedInference: The first feedback influences the chosen model. Independent confirmation requires new evidence after that selection is locked.

figures.visualPremise: Retry from a common committed checkpoint, not mixed local progress
figures.intendedInference: Rank 1 failed after rank 0 advanced. Both must restore the committed checkpoint before retrying the collective.

figures.visualPremise: Correct formatting is not correct policy execution
figures.intendedInference: A response can satisfy the JSON schema while citing stale context or violating policy. Format, knowledge, and behavior need separate checks.

figures.visualPremise: Training signal and update scope form two independent axes
figures.intendedInference: Supervised or preference signals can update all parameters or a parameter-efficient subset. Choosing one axis does not choose the other.

figures.visualPremise: One follow-up can reveal several skills and leave others unknown
figures.intendedInference: A specific follow-up yields evidence about problem framing and experimentation here. Unknown signals remain unknown rather than being inferred from confidence.

figures.visualPremise: Keep the running statistics, discard temporary score tiles
figures.intendedInference: Each key tile updates the row maximum, normalizer, and weighted-value accumulator. The temporary score tile need not survive in HBM.

figures.visualPremise: Remove quadratic intermediate round trips, not all memory movement
figures.intendedInference: The standard route writes and reads the score matrix. Tiled attention still reads inputs and writes outputs while keeping temporary scores on chip.

figures.visualPremise: Manifest membership and actual consumption need different receipts
figures.intendedInference: R17 belongs to the accepted shard and has a training-read receipt. R18 is rejected; its reason remains recorded without membership or consumption.

figures.visualPremise: Known constraints select a drill; unknown permission requires a question
figures.intendedInference: An established time budget can determine exercise size. Unknown tool permission is not an implicit authorization to use tools.

figures.visualPremise: Patch authorship is not ownership of the team rollout
figures.intendedInference: A personal patch proves one contribution. Decision ownership, rollout responsibility, and outcome attribution require their own evidence.

figures.visualPremise: Sharded resting storage still gathers the current unit temporarily
figures.intendedInference: Four ranks each retain one shard at rest. The active wrapped unit gathers for computation, then returns to sharded storage.

figures.visualPremise: Frozen discriminator weights can still transmit generator gradients
figures.intendedInference: The discriminator step stops the fake-sample gradient into G. The generator step freezes D parameters but preserves the path through D.

figures.visualPremise: A supported claim can still be unreleasable
figures.intendedInference: Evidence supports the claim, but release permission is a separate condition. Passing factual support does not authorize disclosure.

figures.visualPremise: Thirteen joint passes do not clear a fourteen-pass floor
figures.intendedInference: Thirteen of twenty trials pass both requirements, or 65%. A 70% floor requires at least fourteen joint passes.

figures.visualPremise: A lexicon update need not retrain the acoustic model
figures.intendedInference: The modular example keeps the acoustic core fixed while changing a separate lexicon. End-to-end systems may place adaptation behind different boundaries.

figures.visualPremise: A nonzero estimate can remain below the worthwhile threshold
figures.intendedInference: A statistically positive half-point gain can still miss a one-point practical threshold. The two questions are distinct.

figures.visualPremise: Length normalization can reverse the raw-probability winner
figures.intendedInference: Raw probability favors A EOS; log-probability divided by length favors A x EOS. Count EOS, exclude BOS, and stop expanding finished beams.

figures.visualPremise: Scanning fewer vectors and storing fewer bytes are different savings
figures.intendedInference: IVF changes which partitions are scanned. PQ compresses their representations; its approximation cannot recover a neighbor excluded by IVF.

figures.visualPremise: Choose an input where rival hypotheses disagree
figures.intendedInference: A shared prediction cannot distinguish the two hypotheses. A predicted output switch is informative, but still does not prove the hidden mechanism uniquely.

figures.visualPremise: Past spending does not enter the forward-value comparison
figures.intendedInference: The illustrative continue option has expected future value 3 and remaining cost 5. Sunk cost 20 cannot turn its net -2 into a benefit.

figures.visualPremise: Local ownership ends where a shared interface changes
figures.intendedInference: An internal implementation choice can remain delegated. Changing a shared interface requires alignment with affected owners rather than unilateral local approval.

figures.visualPremise: A bounded probe branches from a recoverable mainline
figures.intendedInference: Keep the hot mainline recoverable while testing the response. A promising probe needs comparative evidence before replacing that mainline.

figures.visualPremise: A hard failure vetoes quality; order sensitivity requires review
figures.intendedInference: A high quality score cannot override a hard-rule failure. Reversing answer order and changing the judgment exposes a separate calibration problem.

figures.visualPremise: Matching the patient does not match the encounter or approved draft
figures.intendedInference: The patient ID agrees, but the encounter and draft versions differ. A clinician must approve the exact current bundle before release.

figures.visualPremise: A citation proxy can improve while confidentiality fails
figures.intendedInference: More citations do not establish authorized account handling. Independent policy evidence vetoes an apparently improved proxy score.

figures.visualPremise: Caching discounts repeated input, not new output at every call
figures.intendedInference: Each agent call can generate billable output. Repeated cached context changes one cost component, not the whole multi-call total.

figures.visualPremise: Untrusted content can suggest an action without authorizing it
figures.intendedInference: Retrieved text may contain an export instruction. That instruction cannot cross the authority boundary into an executable export.

figures.visualPremise: Paging removes allocation waste, not context or attention growth
figures.intendedInference: Logical KV length and attention reads still grow with context. Paging targets physical allocation waste; it does not eliminate the other two dimensions.

figures.visualPremise: An evaluation-only spike does not identify a training failure
figures.intendedInference: Training loss remains stable while evaluation loss jumps. Investigate evaluation mode, data, and measurement before claiming an optimizer instability.

figures.visualPremise: Change one activation while keeping the corrupted run otherwise fixed
figures.intendedInference: The patched run restores activation A from the clean run. Other corrupted activations stay fixed, isolating this intervention within the declared setup.

figures.visualPremise: A domain gain cannot waive a preservation failure
figures.intendedInference: The probe improves domain loss but fails the declared preservation check. Promotion requires both the gain and preservation conditions.

figures.visualPremise: Unscale before clipping; reject nonfinite updates before stepping
figures.intendedInference: Clipping a scaled gradient uses the wrong effective threshold. A nonfinite result skips the parameter update instead of corrupting the model.

figures.visualPremise: Two active experts do not mean only two stored experts
figures.intendedInference: This token executes E1 and E3. E2 and E4 remain stored even though they perform no work for this token.

figures.visualPremise: Lineage identifies possible exposure; evidence establishes actual impact
figures.intendedInference: A checkpoint descends from the affected shard. A consumption receipt and an outcome check are still needed before claiming actual model harm.

figures.visualPremise: Suppressing one known trigger leaves generalization unknown
figures.intendedInference: The reproduced trigger no longer activates the behavior. Untested paraphrases and contexts remain unknown rather than certified safe.

figures.visualPremise: Separate the decision owned from the outcome shared
figures.intendedInference: A personal design decision is one piece of evidence. Execution contributions and team-level outcomes need distinct attribution rather than being claimed as one personal result.

figures.visualPremise: A bounded critique declares the result that would overturn it
figures.intendedInference: The claim concerns a specific task and matched budget. A contrary matched result would update it; a different task alone would not test the same claim.

figures.visualPremise: Training can see joint information that execution cannot
figures.intendedInference: The centralized critic uses joint state during training. Each deployed actor must act from its allowed local observation without that critic.

figures.visualPremise: The meeting point determines when modalities can interact
figures.intendedInference: Early fusion mixes modalities before shared processing. Late fusion keeps representations separate until their scores or decisions meet.

figures.visualPremise: A similar relevant item is not a valid hard negative
figures.intendedInference: High similarity establishes hardness, not irrelevance. The label gate must reject a relevant answer before negative training uses it.

figures.visualPremise: A nonzero gradient does not prove that the intended weights changed
figures.intendedInference: The recipe produces gradient 0.8 but observed parameter change zero. Check the actual optimizer-bound parameters and step receipt.

figures.visualPremise: Training assignment and inference suppression solve different problems
figures.intendedInference: Training matches predictions to ground-truth supervision. Inference removes redundant predicted boxes without access to ground truth.

figures.visualPremise: Less work saves time only when it shortens the critical path
figures.intendedInference: Parallel tasks A=100 and B=60 finish together after 100 units. Halving B still takes 100; reducing A to 80 lowers the finish time.

figures.visualPremise: Logical order survives scattered physical placement
figures.intendedInference: Logical blocks 0,1,2 map to physical pages 7,2,9. The block table, not physical adjacency, reconstructs the token sequence.

figures.visualPremise: Co-purchase evidence does not establish product compatibility
figures.intendedInference: A frequently co-purchased case can still fail the phone fit requirement. Complementarity needs a separate compatibility relation.

figures.visualPremise: A later ranker cannot recover a missing upstream candidate
figures.intendedInference: The relevant candidate survives retrieval but fails an earlier cap. The final ranker can compare only the candidates it receives.

figures.visualPremise: Idle stage-slots are unused capacity, not extra elapsed time
figures.intendedInference: Three microbatches cross three stages in five time slots. Six idle stage-slots occur within that same elapsed schedule.

figures.visualPremise: Model shards do not multiply distinct training examples
figures.intendedInference: Two data replicas, sixteen examples per microbatch, and four accumulation steps produce 128 distinct examples. Tensor and pipeline shards share those examples.

figures.visualPremise: A tested reward proxy can become untested after optimization
figures.intendedInference: The proxy was validated on the original response distribution. Optimization shifts responses, so original accuracy does not certify the new region.

figures.visualPremise: One weight load can serve more than one token computation
figures.intendedInference: Prefill or batching can reuse loaded weights across tokens. Decode still performs token-specific computation and reads its growing cache.

figures.visualPremise: The awaited dependency can dominate a faster model
figures.intendedInference: A response waits for parallel dependencies A=100 and model B=60. Halving model time leaves the awaited 100-unit dependency unchanged.

figures.visualPremise: Only communication beyond useful overlap extends the step
figures.intendedInference: A 40-unit collective overlaps 30 units of useful work. Its exposed tail is 10, not the full 40.

figures.visualPremise: A resolvable citation can still fail to support its claim
figures.intendedInference: Both citations resolve to documents. Only citation A supports the exact claim; citation B must not pass merely because its link works.

figures.visualPremise: Keep the answer connected to one versioned source chunk
figures.intendedInference: A stable chunk identity and version connect the retrieved evidence to its source. A citation string alone is not that lineage receipt.

figures.visualPremise: A fast request can still use an old feature snapshot
figures.intendedInference: The request completes quickly after reading a much earlier snapshot. Request latency and feature freshness use different timestamp differences.

figures.visualPremise: A generated recommendation must satisfy deadline and catalog gates
figures.intendedInference: A timely suggestion for an unknown item fails the catalog gate. A valid but late suggestion also falls back to the bounded baseline.

figures.visualPremise: Rejected savings do not become the next baseline
figures.intendedInference: The 8-unit change passes quality and replaces the 10-unit baseline. The 6-unit change fails tail quality, so the accepted baseline stays 8.

figures.visualPremise: An observed gap does not identify a unique cause
figures.intendedInference: The same train/validation gap can accompany leakage, distribution shift, or overfitting. A discriminating check precedes the choice of regularizer.

figures.visualPremise: Unequal tuning opportunities confound the method comparison
figures.intendedInference: Method B received ten times the search trials. Its best score cannot isolate the method effect without a matched tuning comparison.

figures.visualPremise: A successful final state can fail the required process
figures.intendedInference: The environment reaches the goal while violating an allowed-tool constraint. The grader must retain both outcome and process evidence.

figures.visualPremise: DPO reuses preference pairs without a separate reward-model rollout loop
figures.intendedInference: Both routes use preference information. DPO directly optimizes on pairs; the illustrated RLHF route adds reward-model fitting and policy rollouts.

figures.visualPremise: Ask the expert about the state the learner actually reached
figures.intendedInference: The learner drifts away from the demonstration state. DAgger labels that visited state so the dataset includes corrective decisions there.

figures.visualPremise: Competent evaluation and adversarial containment are separate assumptions
figures.intendedInference: A judge can identify harmful behavior yet fail to contain the acting system. Test detection and control with independent evidence.

figures.visualPremise: A complaint sample proposes a scope; a bounded check tests it
figures.intendedInference: The observed complaints concern one slice. A discriminating sample from other slices decides whether the proposed scope should widen.

figures.visualPremise: The first rejected draft invalidates its dependent suffix
figures.intendedInference: After accepting A and rejecting draft B, later draft C cannot survive unchanged. Draw the corrected replacement and restart from the valid prefix.

figures.visualPremise: Visible partial words remain revisable until commitment
figures.intendedInference: The partial hypothesis changes as audio arrives. Only the declared finalization rule turns a provisional token sequence into committed output.

figures.visualPremise: A shorter run can spend more accelerator-hours
figures.intendedInference: Eight devices for two hours cost sixteen device-hours. Sixteen devices for 1.5 hours finish sooner but cost twenty-four device-hours.

figures.visualPremise: Filtering training rows is not independent final evaluation
figures.intendedInference: A training-row judge can filter synthetic examples. Reusing the same feedback for final selection does not supply independent confirmation.

figures.visualPremise: First-layer channels partition; second-layer contributions add
figures.intendedInference: Two channel shards produce partial outputs 4 and 6 for one coordinate. The full coordinate is their sum 10, not their concatenation.

figures.visualPremise: Generating a correct answer is insufficient if the verifier rejects it
figures.intendedInference: Candidate A is correct but discarded; B is wrong but selected. More generation alone does not repair this selection bottleneck.

figures.visualPremise: Different parallelism axes partition different objects
figures.intendedInference: Data replicas partition examples; pipeline stages partition layers; tensor shards partition computations. Optimizer-state sharding changes stored ownership rather than example count.

figures.visualPremise: Stored experts and active token computation belong in different ledgers
figures.intendedInference: In a four-expert top-two model, all four expert weights remain stored. A single token executes only its two selected experts.

figures.visualPremise: Item encoding happens before the request; query encoding happens during it
figures.intendedInference: Offline item vectors populate the index. The live request encodes its query and searches that versioned index without re-encoding every item.

figures.visualPremise: Joint encoding spends work only on the retrieved candidate set
figures.intendedInference: A two-tower stage retrieves K=20 from 1,000 items. The cross-encoder scores those twenty pairs; it cannot rescue an item outside them.

figures.visualPremise: Generation has no observed input to encode
figures.intendedInference: Training infers z from observed x through the encoder. Generation instead samples z from the prior and decodes it without q(z|x).

figures.visualPremise: Accepted tokens must repay draft and verification work
figures.intendedInference: With target verification cost 1 and three draft costs of 0.1, two accepted tokens cost 0.65 each. One accepted token would cost 1.3, exceeding baseline 1.

figures.visualPremise: A split is valid only for the dependency the claim must respect
figures.intendedInference: Random rows test a different claim from unseen users or future deployment. Select the boundary before interpreting the held-out score.

figures.visualPremise: A cooldown branch does not have to replace the hot mainline
figures.intendedInference: A checkpoint forks into a continued hot run and a cooldown evaluation branch. Their lineage is shared; promotion remains a separate decision.

figures.visualPremise: The modes share context, not tool permission
figures.intendedInference: Inline, chat, and review remain nonexecuting modes. The isolated agent receives only its explicitly scoped tool authority.

figures.visualPremise: Cancellation withdraws authority before it proves worker termination
figures.intendedInference: The request cancels future dispatch immediately. A later worker-stop receipt establishes termination; neither event means the patch was successfully verified.

figures.visualPremise: Completed shards still need permission and validation before publication
figures.intendedInference: Artifact completion alone does not authorize use. Policy permission and passing validation must both join the completed artifact before release.

figures.visualPremise: Permission is not an occurrence receipt
figures.intendedInference: Correlated receipt confirms occurrence.

figures.visualPremise: Old-epoch packets stay invalid
figures.intendedInference: Retired-epoch packets stay rejected.

figures.visualPremise: Rollback restores a compatible bundle, not just an old model
figures.intendedInference: Model version 1 cannot be paired blindly with version-2 features and policy. Restore the verified compatible model-feature-policy bundle.

figures.visualPremise: Every path belongs to exactly one last-move group
figures.intendedInference: Five paths end with one step; three end with two steps. The disjoint groups sum to eight paths up five stairs.

figures.visualPremise: One completed parent still leaves the other prerequisite unmet
figures.intendedInference: Course 3 requires courses 1 and 2. Its unmet count falls from two to one to zero, becoming ready only at zero.

figures.visualPremise: Taking the current house excludes its immediate neighbor
figures.intendedInference: For values (2,7,9,3), skipping house 3 keeps 11. Taking it adds 3 only to the earlier optimum 7, giving 10.

figures.visualPremise: A match extends the diagonal, not an arbitrary neighbor
figures.intendedInference: For AB versus ACB, matching B extends diagonal value 1 to 2. At mismatch C, compare the up and left subproblems instead.

figures.visualPremise: The new item can extend the old sums only once
figures.intendedInference: Starting from old sums (0,1), item 5 creates only (5,6). Ten is absent because a newly created five cannot reuse that same item.

figures.visualPremise: Path compression changes bookkeeping, not the original graph
figures.intendedInference: Finding node 4 redirects its parent from 3 to root 1. The accepted problem edges remain unchanged.

figures.visualPremise: Increasing choice indices erase duplicate orderings
figures.intendedInference: Indices 0 then 1 generate subset (1,2). Attempting 1 then 0 goes backward and would duplicate the same membership.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: one comparison rejects a whole row of pairs
figures.intendedInference: With fixed -4 and left -2, even partner 2 gives -4. Every smaller partner also fails, so discard that left value.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: only the first unequal character creates an ordering edge
figures.intendedInference: The words wrt and wrf first differ at their third character. Infer t before f; the shared prefix supplies no new edge.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a failed child cannot be repaired by a balanced parent
figures.intendedInference: A child returns the unbalanced sentinel, not a usable height. Propagate that failure rather than averaging or comparing it as a valid depth.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the saved trade survives a worse current selling day
figures.intendedInference: Prices (3,1,5,2) produce best profit 4 at price 5. The final price gives current profit 1 but does not erase the saved 4.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: one hit count has two denominators
figures.intendedInference: Eight true positives accompany two misses and 32 false alarms. Recall is 8/10; precision is 8/40.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the comparison removes an entire sorted region
figures.intendedInference: For target 7 in (1,3,5,7,9), middle value 5 is too small. Every value at or left of that middle is also too small.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: freeze the current level before enqueueing its children
figures.intendedInference: The level begins with A and B, so process exactly two nodes. Newly appended children belong to the next level.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a winning path may branch, but the returned path may not
figures.intendedInference: At value 10 with positive child gains 4 and 6, the local complete path scores 20. The upward return is 16, using only one child.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: future positions receive zero weight
figures.intendedInference: A query at position 1 can use positions 0 and 1 only. Masked future entries contribute exactly zero to the output.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the final move partitions paths into disjoint groups
figures.intendedInference: For five stairs, five paths end with one step and three with two. These groups do not overlap, so their counts add to eight.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a cycle reuses the already-created copy
figures.intendedInference: When B reaches A again, the original-to-copy map returns A-prime. Linking to original A would corrupt the clone boundary.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: an unreachable predecessor supplies no valid solution
figures.intendedInference: For coins (2,3) and amount 3, coin 2 points to unreachable amount 1. Coin 3 points to base amount 0 and supplies count 1.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: group ordered sequences by their last value
figures.intendedInference: With values (1,2) and target 4, group by last value. Three sequences end in 1; two end in 2.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: reuse a value without returning to an earlier choice index
figures.intendedInference: For candidates (2,3), path (2,2,3) is allowed. Path (3,2,2) would duplicate the same combination and requires a backward index move.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: preorder selects the root; inorder assigns subtree membership
figures.intendedInference: Preorder begins with 3. Inorder (9,3,15,20,7) places 9 on its left and the remaining three nodes on its right.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: keeping the shorter wall cannot improve its current limit
figures.intendedInference: With shorter wall 2 and width 3, area is 6. Moving only the taller wall makes width 2 and height at most 2, so area is at most 4.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: repeated positions collapse to one set entry
figures.intendedInference: The input has four positions but only three distinct values. The unequal counts prove a duplicate without needing to sort.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: fix the last endpoint of (2,2,2,1,1,1)
figures.intendedInference: Six starts contain at most three odds. Two contain at most two odds. Their difference leaves four starts containing exactly three.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: reuse the halved number and add its low bit
figures.intendedInference: Binary 1101 has the count of 110 plus one. Thus count(13)=count(6)+1=3.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a course is ready only when its final prerequisite disappears
figures.intendedInference: Course 3 has prerequisites 1 and 2. Emitting only 1 leaves its unmet count at one; emitting 2 then makes it ready.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: an empty ready queue is not enough to prove success
figures.intendedInference: Both cases have an empty queue. Only the case that emitted all courses succeeds; remaining courses indicate a cycle.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the target logit matters even when the normalizer is shared
figures.intendedInference: For logits (2,0), log-sum-exp is about 2.127. Choosing class 0 gives loss 0.127; choosing class 1 gives 2.127.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a wait is an index difference, not a temperature difference
figures.intendedInference: Index 0 stores 70 degrees; index 3 stores 80. The warmer day arrives three days later, not ten days later.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: finish the inner repeat before applying its outer multiplier
figures.intendedInference: For 2[a3[b]], first decode 3[b] to bbb. Then repeat the completed abbb twice.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: zero is allowed in 10, not as the leading digit of 01
figures.intendedInference: The pair 10 maps to a letter, while 01 is invalid. The two-digit transition must satisfy the actual range 10 through 26.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a matching prefix is not automatically a stored word
figures.intendedInference: The trie contains bad. Prefix ba exists, but its final node is not terminal; wildcard b.d reaches the terminal for bad.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a mismatch pays one edit; a match inherits the diagonal
figures.intendedInference: For single characters a and b, substitution costs one. Matching a against a adds zero to the empty-prefix diagonal.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: length, not delimiter appearance, determines the payload boundary
figures.intendedInference: Encoding a#b as 3#a#b preserves its internal #. Read exactly three payload characters after the length delimiter.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: balanced heap sizes still need the ordering invariant
figures.intendedInference: Heaps (5) and (1) have equal sizes but reversed ordering. Swapping their tops restores max(left)<=min(right) before reading the median.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the middle remains a candidate when it lies on the low side
figures.intendedInference: For (3,4,1,2), first discard middle 4 and its left side. Next, middle 1 is below rightmost 2: set right=mid, keeping that middle as the minimum candidate.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the edge count alone cannot rule out a cycle plus isolation
figures.intendedInference: A triangle on three nodes plus one isolated node has n-1 edges for n=4. It is not a tree because connectivity fails.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: equal lengths do not imply equal character counts
figures.intendedInference: Both ab and ba count one a and one b. By contrast, aa counts two a characters.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: two linear cases prevent taking both circular endpoints
figures.intendedInference: For a circle, solve once without the last house and once without the first. Every valid solution belongs to at least one of these cases.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: taking the current house can reuse only the earlier nonadjacent optimum
figures.intendedInference: At index 3 of (2,7,9,3), skip gives 11. Taking the current value gives best-through-index-1 plus 3, or 10.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: prefix reachability and word membership are separate flags
figures.intendedInference: After inserting apple, app is a valid prefix but not yet a word. Inserting app changes its terminal flag without rebuilding the shared path.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: merge the overlap but stop before the first separated interval
figures.intendedInference: Inserting (2,5) into (1,3),(6,9) merges only the first interval. The separated (6,9) stays unchanged.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: swap subtree positions without changing their stored values
figures.intendedInference: Root 1 keeps value 1 while its returned left and right children exchange positions. Replacing values alone is not the recursive subtree operation.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: an unreachable index cannot donate its large jump
figures.intendedInference: For (1,0,9), the reachable frontier stops at index 1. The large value at index 2 is never reachable and cannot extend that frontier.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a passing speed rules out the need for faster candidates
figures.intendedInference: For piles (3,6,7,11) and eight hours, speed 3 needs ten hours. Speed 4 needs eight and is feasible; every lower speed fails.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the kth largest is the smallest value in the retained top-k heap
figures.intendedInference: For k=3 and values (7,2,9,4), retain (4,7,9). Its smallest value 4 is third largest, not the global minimum 2.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: count a node when inorder visits it, not when it enters the stack
figures.intendedInference: A root 2 can enter the stack before its left child 1. The visit order is still 1 then 2 then 3.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a shorter bar closes spans but the zero sentinel remains
figures.intendedInference: After heights (2,1,2) and a zero sentinel, positive spans are resolved. The actual stack still retains the zero sentinel; it is not an empty stack.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: compare node identity, not repeated stored values
figures.intendedInference: Two distinct nodes may both store value 7. A cycle witness requires the slow and fast pointers to reach the same node identity after valid moves.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a matching pair extends the diagonal subproblem
figures.intendedInference: For AB versus ACB, B matches B and extends diagonal 1 to 2. A mismatch compares the two shorter-prefix answers instead.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: start a run only where no predecessor exists
figures.intendedInference: For set (1,2,3,8), start at 1 and 8. Starting again at 2 or 3 repeats work inside the already-covered run.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a cached suffix can serve more than one starting point
figures.intendedInference: Paths starting at 1 and 2 can both enter suffix (3,4). The suffix length is solved once and reused; the path still follows strictly increasing values.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a smaller tail preserves length but is not the saved subsequence
figures.intendedInference: Processing (3,5,7,2) changes the length-one tail to 2. Tails (2,5,7) are extension bounds, not a subsequence of that processed input.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a shorter new palindrome cannot replace the saved best
figures.intendedInference: A saved palindrome of length 5 remains best when a later center finds length 3. Update only when the new length is strictly larger under this tie rule.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the saved best need not describe the final shown window
figures.intendedInference: AABA needs one replacement and has length 4. A later ABBA window needs two; it does not invalidate the earlier saved optimum of 4.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: an old duplicate cannot move the left boundary backward
figures.intendedInference: In abba, the last a was at index 0 while left already equals 2. Set left=max(2,0+1)=2 rather than reopening the duplicate b.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: stop when the targets split or one equals the current node
figures.intendedInference: At node 6 with targets 2 and 8, their search directions split. If one target is 6 itself, that same node is already the ancestor.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a read changes the victim of the next eviction
figures.intendedInference: With key 1 older than key 2, reading 1 moves it to most-recent position. Inserting key 3 then evicts key 2.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: add this node to the larger returned child depth
figures.intendedInference: Child depths 2 and 4 produce parent depth 5. Adding both child depths would count nodes from different root-to-leaf paths.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a negative minimum becomes a positive maximum after a sign flip
figures.intendedInference: For (-2,3,-4), the previous minimum -6 becomes 24 after multiplying by -4. Retaining only the previous maximum would lose this answer.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the saved best survives a losing final extension
figures.intendedInference: For (-2,3,4,-10), the final current sum is -3. The saved best remains 7 from subarray (3,4).

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the peak room demand survives a smaller final active heap
figures.intendedInference: Meetings (0,2),(.5,1.5),(3,4) overlap two at a time near t=1. After removing finished meetings, the final heap holds only one. Two rooms are still required for the saved peak.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: touching endpoints are not overlapping meeting interiors
figures.intendedInference: The test is next_start<previous_end. Equality permits attendance; a strictly earlier start creates a conflict.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: extend the active endpoint before comparing the next interval
figures.intendedInference: Intervals (1,4) and (2,6) merge to (1,6). The later (5,7) overlaps that updated endpoint, so all three merge to (1,7).

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: advance the list that supplied the minimum, then compare again
figures.intendedInference: Current heads are (1,4,2). After emitting 1 and exposing 9, the next minimum is 2, not the next value from that same list.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the untouched remainder is already sorted
figures.intendedInference: After one input is exhausted, append the other input head directly. Its internal links already represent the correctly ordered suffix.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: duplicate minima need duplicate historical state
figures.intendedInference: Pushing 5,2,2 stores minima 5,2,2. Popping one 2 must leave minimum 2; recording only distinct minima would incorrectly restore 5.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: bounded half-open slicing preserves a short tail
figures.intendedInference: Seven items and batch size 3 yield lengths 3,3,1. The last slice keeps item 6 rather than dropping or duplicating it.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: matching all character types is not enough when demand repeats
figures.intendedInference: Target AABC needs two copies of A. Candidate ABC contains every character type but misses one required A.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: paired XOR terms cancel and leave the absent value
figures.intendedInference: For n=3, observations (3,0,1) omit value 2. XORing observations against the full range (0,1,2,3) leaves only that unpaired value.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a queued estimate is stale when a shorter distance is already known
figures.intendedInference: Two entries can name the same node. With best distance 2, a later popped entry carrying distance 6 is stale and must not expand neighbors.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the earlier finish preserves more future choices
figures.intendedInference: Keeping (1,3) permits the next interval (3,4). Keeping (1,5) blocks it, despite the identical starting point.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: each pass clears exactly the lowest remaining one bit
figures.intendedInference: Binary 1100 becomes 1000, then 0000 under n&(n-1). Two passes count two set bits, not four bit positions.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: only a successful union reduces the component count
figures.intendedInference: Four nodes begin as four components. Joining (0,1) and (2,3) leaves two; joining (1,0) again does not reduce that count.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: mark a discovered cell before another neighbor discovers it again
figures.intendedInference: From the top-left cell, two neighbors share the bottom-right cell. Marking on discovery puts that shared cell into the traversal once.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: reverse search walks uphill to find possible downhill sources
figures.intendedInference: Starting from an ocean, reverse traversal may move from height 2 to 5. Moving to height 1 reverses the intended reachability rule.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: equal token values can have different validity
figures.intendedInference: For sequences (0,7) and (4), the first zero is real data. The padded second-row zero is invalid; sequence lengths define the mask.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: combine row norms with the cross-product, without a 3D difference tensor
figures.intendedInference: For x=(1,2) and y=(3,2), squared distance is 5+13-2x7=4. The broadcasted identity produces that same scalar.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: count locations, not just distinct palindrome texts
figures.intendedInference: String aaa has three length-one, two length-two, and one length-three palindromic substrings. These are six occurrences, not three distinct strings.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: descending sums prevent one item from being reused in its own update
figures.intendedInference: From reachable sum 0, processing one item of value 2 may add sum 2 only. Forward iteration could incorrectly reuse it to make 4.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: character multiplicities must match, not only membership
figures.intendedInference: Patterns aab and window abb share the same character set. Their counts differ, so the window is not a permutation.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: unused positions remain available regardless of their original order
figures.intendedInference: After choosing values (1,3) from (1,2,3), value 2 is still unused. An increasing-start rule would wrongly exclude that valid permutation.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: left and right products exclude exactly the current position
figures.intendedInference: For (2,0,4), prefix and suffix products produce (0,8,0). The middle output is nonzero even though its own input is zero.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the closing edge connects nodes already in one component
figures.intendedInference: After joining (1,2) and (2,3), nodes 1 and 3 share a representative. Their new edge closes a cycle instead of merging components.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the dummy predecessor makes deleting the head an ordinary splice
figures.intendedInference: For (1,2,3) and n=3, the predecessor is the dummy node. Its next link skips node 1 and returns head 2.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: reverse the detached second half before weaving
figures.intendedInference: Split after node 3 and reverse the detached second half. Alternating the detached halves yields (1,5,2,4,3) without a cycle.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: fixed-width reversal maps position i to position 31-i
figures.intendedInference: For a 32-bit input containing only low bit 0, reversal sets high bit 31. The result is 2147483648; leading zeros still count as positions.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: save the remaining chain before reversing the current link
figures.intendedInference: Before redirecting node 1 toward null, save its original next node 2. That saved reference is the only route to the unprocessed suffix.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: transpose then reverse each row rotates coordinates clockwise
figures.intendedInference: Input rows (1,2) and (3,4) rotate to (3,1) and (4,2). Reversing columns after transposing would rotate the other direction.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: each frozen queue layer advances time by one minute
figures.intendedInference: This example reaches its last fresh orange at minute 4. Cells in the same wave share a time; six infections do not imply six minutes.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: equal values in different child positions are not the same tree
figures.intendedInference: Both trees visit values 1 then 2 in preorder without null markers. Their left and right shapes differ, so structural equality is false.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: identify the sorted half before testing whether it contains the target
figures.intendedInference: For target 0, the sorted half (4,5,6,7) is ineligible. Keep opposite half (0,1,2).

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: null markers preserve the child positions that values alone lose
figures.intendedInference: A left child and a right child can share value preorder (1,2). Their null-marked encodings differ and reconstruct distinct shapes.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: new zeros must not create new row or column obligations
figures.intendedInference: The only original zero is at row 0, column 1. Final row 1 stays (1,0,1), not all zeros.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a crossed boundary prevents revisiting a one-row remainder
figures.intendedInference: For a single row (1,2,3), the top traversal consumes every cell. The bottom traversal must be skipped after top passes bottom.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the capacity predicate becomes feasible at the correct boundary
figures.intendedInference: For (7,2,5,10,8), capacity 17 needs three groups; capacity 18 needs two. With k=2, choose the first feasible capacity, 18.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: subtracting the maximum preserves probabilities while preventing overflow
figures.intendedInference: Logits (1000,1001) shift to (-1,0). Their softmax probabilities are about 0.269 and 0.731 without exponentiating 1000.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: query the old prefix frequency before inserting the current prefix
figures.intendedInference: For input (0) and target 0, the seeded empty prefix contributes one matching subarray. Inserting the current prefix first would incorrectly count two.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: each position supplies one independent include-or-exclude choice
figures.intendedInference: For values (1,2), four binary choice paths produce four distinct subsets. Excluding a value is a branch, not an omitted decision.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: equal candidate roots still require a complete local tree match
figures.intendedInference: Both candidate roots store 5 and have left child 3. An extra right child 7 means the larger local tree is not equal to the proposed subtree.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: simultaneous XOR and shifted-AND updates preserve the total
figures.intendedInference: For 5+3, provisional sum and carry remain separate until carry is zero. Each row still totals 8 within the fixed-width word.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: evict by frequency, not by the value itself
figures.intendedInference: For k=2, frequencies are 9:3, 1:5, and 8:4. Keep values 1 and 8; the smallest retained frequency is 4.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: partition selects membership; it does not sort the selected candidates
figures.intendedInference: Candidate indices (3,1) have correct membership but no score order. Sorting that subset returns indices (1,3).

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: lookup before insertion prevents pairing an item with itself
figures.intendedInference: For target 6 and input (3,3), the first 3 cannot match itself. The second 3 finds the earlier index 0 and returns distinct indices.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: the final move partitions paths by their incoming neighbor
figures.intendedInference: In a 3-by-3 grid, three paths arrive from above and three from the left. The disjoint final-move groups sum to six.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: equal length does not guarantee equal multiplicities
figures.intendedInference: Strings aab and abb both have length 3. Their character counts differ, so they are not anagrams.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: skip non-alphanumeric characters before comparing the ends
figures.intendedInference: For A,b:a, normalization gives aba. The punctuation never participates in an equality comparison; the retained letters match from both ends.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a closing bracket must match the most recent opener
figures.intendedInference: For ([)], the ) encounters [ on top. A matching ( deeper in the stack does not make the sequence valid.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a descendant must satisfy every inherited ancestor bound
figures.intendedInference: Node 12 fits above parent 5 but violates ancestor 10. Every descendant in that ancestor's left subtree must remain below 10.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a tempting longest prefix can leave an impossible suffix
figures.intendedInference: For cars and dictionary (car,ca,rs), greedy car leaves invalid s. The valid split is ca plus rs; reachability must consider both boundaries.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a terminal trie node may still have another word below it
figures.intendedInference: Emit a at its terminal node, then keep exploring. For adjacent cells a,b and words (a,ab), continuing finds ab.

figures.visualPremise: Worked example: a matching letter cannot reuse a cell already on this path
figures.intendedInference: On a two-cell board A,B, target ABA would require cell 0 twice. The final A matches in value but is unavailable on the active path.

mentalPictureEdition.target: Fiftyfold ambition; no measured learner-gain claim
limitations: Fiftyfold is an editorial ambition, not a measured learner outcome; no learner study or publication-standard certification.
Every final phone primary was individually reviewed; not every authored execution state or every theme image was manually inspected.
All physical PDFs pass bounds, proof-word completeness, tagging and same-page composition checks; nine complete physical figure pages were directly viewed.
New drawers have local numeric/identity assertions; inherited legacy arithmetic tests exercise the retained original bodies, not every new drawing independently.
Raw native PNGs are authenticated files, not a claim that every crop was manually inspected; nine dark sample crops are superseded by geometry-stable captures.
This edition authorizes a local commit, not another push or publication.

figures.title: Only 99 of 1,098 positive results come from the diseased group
figures.authoredReview: The result-only cohorts hide the base rate. Preserve cohort identity through unequal selection and normalization.
figures.prediction: If disease prevalence rises, which input cohort changes before the test acts?

individualReview.observation: The original cohort, two positive-selection filters, and the renormalized 99/1098 group are visibly distinct; prevalence and sensitivity cannot be confused with the posterior.

figures.title: Twice the noise needs four times the sample here
figures.authoredReview: Sample-budget bars do not show why the factor is squared. Turn doubled noise width into four equal variance tiles.
figures.prediction: Tripling noise requires how many baseline sample budgets under the same assumptions?

individualReview.observation: Doubling the noise width creates four equal area tiles and four sample budgets; the fixed-effect and fixed-error assumptions remain visible.

figures.title: AdamW gives equal weights equal explicit decay despite different histories
figures.authoredReview: Equal result bars omit the route. Put coupled decay through the preconditioner and let direct decay visibly bypass it.
figures.prediction: Which route changes when only the frozen preconditioner changes?

individualReview.observation: Direct reinspection shows clear space between the repaired blue arrows and 0.001/0.0001 labels, while both green bypass routes still end at 0.001.

figures.title: A larger value can outweigh a smaller attention weight
figures.authoredReview: Endpoint bars omit the multiplication. Let weight set width and scalar value set height so contribution is area.
figures.prediction: What becomes of the second contribution if its value is zero but its weight stays unchanged?

individualReview.observation: The smaller green weight owns a taller value rectangle; the shared 0.2 tiles visibly sum the 0.8 and 2 contributions to 2.8.

figures.title: Balanced training rows do not make real-world positives equally common
figures.authoredReview: A deployment-only population omits the sampling intervention. Pull a balanced batch out of the unchanged imbalanced world.
figures.prediction: Does drawing equal class counts change the deployment base rate?

individualReview.observation: The shortened balanced-batch heading now clears both selection lines; ten positive and ten negative training examples do not alter the visible 10/990 world population.

figures.title: Eight hits can mean high recall and low precision
figures.authoredReview: A table hides membership. Select two different subsets of the same cases while preserving the eight shared hits.
figures.prediction: Which extra cases enter precision but not recall?

individualReview.observation: Actual-positive and predicted-positive groups preserve the same eight hits, while their different miss/false-alarm inventories expose eighty-percent recall versus twenty-percent precision.

figures.title: An 80% forecast bin needs an 80% observed positive rate
figures.authoredReview: Observed outcomes alone omit the forecast. Compare the expected aggregate count with the actual aggregate count on one scale.
figures.prediction: If 80 cases were positive, would this bin still show the same calibration gap?

individualReview.observation: The forecast and observed hundred-case bars share one scale, so eighty predicted versus sixty observed leaves a visibly twenty-case calibration gap.

figures.title: Zero logging probability leaves action C's reward unidentified
figures.authoredReview: A missing value needs a missing path, not another ledger entry. Give the zero-probability action no route to an observed reward.
figures.prediction: Can multiplying observed A and B records reveal C rewards?

individualReview.observation: A and B have live logging paths, while C has a broken zero-probability path and an unknown reward rather than a fabricated zero.

figures.title: Refill B's finished slot with C on the next iteration
figures.authoredReview: Ledger rows obscure persistence. Keep A in the same slot while B exits and C enters the released slot.
figures.prediction: Must A finish before C can occupy B’s released slot?

individualReview.observation: Reinspection shows the running label and next-iteration heading clear of A's preserved route; B leaves and C enters only the freed neighboring slot.

figures.title: An event before noon can still arrive too late for the noon prediction
figures.authoredReview: Isolated timestamp dots hide the unavailable interval. Carry one record from event to availability across the prediction boundary.
figures.prediction: Can a later-arriving record be used because its event happened earlier?

individualReview.observation: The one record's event point precedes noon but its availability point follows noon, visibly preventing a late arrival from entering the earlier prediction.

figures.title: Declared costs and review limits turn risk scores into different actions
figures.authoredReview: One policy map can look universal. Keep one score fixed while changing the declared action regions.
figures.prediction: Does a fixed score contain a policy-independent action?

individualReview.observation: The score marker stays at 0.85 on both equal rulers while the declared policy bands change its action from block to review.

figures.title: Extra training takes six points from post-training, not protected reserves
figures.authoredReview: The transfer should be countable and the protected accounts visible. Reassign six identified budget units while retaining the other 94.
figures.prediction: Which account gives up the six points, and which two accounts do not move?

individualReview.observation: The six circled tokens change ownership from post-training to training, with serving and recovery unchanged and both populations totaling 100.

figures.title: Shrink candidates before spending expensive scoring work
figures.authoredReview: Three bars do not show survivors. Reuse candidate positions through two filters, with one tile representing 100 candidates.
figures.prediction: Can final scoring recover a candidate removed upstream?

individualReview.observation: The same hundred-candidate marks fade from 10000 retrieved to 1000 shortlisted to 100 scored; eliminated members have no downstream scoring route.

figures.title: The next valid-looking action can still breach the aggregate impact limit
figures.authoredReview: An overflow result omits the proposal being inserted. Preserve the committed prefix and expose the ten-unit excess at the wall.
figures.prediction: Does refusing the proposal reverse the committed effects?

individualReview.observation: The sixty committed and fifty proposed segments extend ten units beyond the actual hundred-unit wall; rejection preserves the already committed prefix.

figures.title: The shared memory limit rejects the faster but oversized cache
figures.authoredReview: Memory is a physical admission boundary. Align both cache choices with the same eight-slot wall and leave the ninth unit outside.
figures.prediction: Can a speed advantage make the ninth memory unit fit?

individualReview.observation: The observed local decision remains a green claim, while the separate downstream rollout question mark prevents acceptance from becoming evidence of durable implementation.

figures.title: A frame received 0.10 seconds ago can still be 4.30 seconds old
figures.authoredReview: Age bars do not show identity. Carry the same stamped frame through transport and measure both ages from the same question.
figures.prediction: Can fast delivery refresh an old capture?

individualReview.observation: The same captured frame reaches the arrival icon, but its 4.30-second content-age span remains separate from the 0.10-second arrival-age span.

figures.title: Free compute cannot substitute for missing KV pages
figures.authoredReview: Yes/no tokens hide independent resources. Make compute and KV separate banks whose gates must both pass.
figures.prediction: Can two free compute units supply the missing KV page?

individualReview.observation: Compute uses four of six slots but KV requires six against five available slots; the unmatched sixth KV page stays beyond the wall, so spare compute cannot supply the missing resource.

figures.title: Only displayed items create exposure records for this request
figures.authoredReview: Flat groups hide nested selection. Retain the same 100 candidate identities through eligibility and exposure filters.
figures.prediction: What reward is observed for an eligible candidate that was never shown?

individualReview.observation: The same hundred candidate positions narrow to twenty eligible and five shown; fifteen eligible but unshown members remain without exposure labels rather than becoming negative outcomes.

figures.title: Immediate viewer response precedes the full creator-supply observation window
figures.authoredReview: One event list hides two response speeds. Split viewer and creator lanes across the short-experiment stop boundary.
figures.prediction: Can the early readout rule out an effect whose observation lies after the test?

individualReview.observation: Viewer response occurs before the marked short-test end while creator response occurs after it on the same event clock; the early readout cannot exclude the later effect or quantify its duration.

figures.title: Flat activation regions weaken the gradient travelling backward
figures.authoredReview: Derivative curves do not show what a local slope measures. Draw forward responses and equal input nudges whose vertical changes differ.
figures.prediction: Where does the same small input move produce almost no output change?

individualReview.observation: Forward sigmoid/ReLU shapes and separately identified local slopes make the flat-region mechanism visible without presenting slopes as outputs.

figures.title: The basin gets sharper without changing the model's predictions
figures.authoredReview: Keep one physical scalar prediction while changing its ruler labels. The same displacement receives a smaller coordinate value and a larger coordinate curvature.
figures.prediction: Does relabeling a=2b alter the represented scalar prediction?

individualReview.observation: Aligned rulers map a=2 to b=1 for the same prediction and loss, while the coordinate-curvature caveat explicitly prevents a sharpness-invariance claim.

figures.title: An allowed small move can still cross the decision boundary
figures.authoredReview: A line between points hides the allowance. Draw both decision regions and the permitted horizontal interval around the original point.
figures.prediction: Can an allowance of 0.2 cross the boundary from x=0.3?

individualReview.observation: The original and perturbed points sit on opposite sides of the dashed decision boundary, with the horizontal allowance distinguished from the whole geometric scene.

figures.title: Hold one factor matrix still while solving rows of the other
figures.authoredReview: Alternation is a freeze-and-solve operation, not two moving factor tables. Hold one rank-one item vector while two independent user rows settle.
figures.prediction: Which factor must stay fixed while these user rows are solved?

individualReview.observation: Both user solves receive the same frozen V=(1,2), and separate 2/3 outputs reconstruct their own ratings without changing that factor.

figures.title: The same upstream gradient meets different cached multipliers
figures.authoredReview: A final pair of gradients hides the cached multipliers. Fork the upstream signal through the other forward input.
figures.prediction: If x doubles while the upstream signal stays fixed, which parameter gradient doubles?

individualReview.observation: The shared upstream four meets cached two or three in separate reverse products, yielding eight and twelve rather than repeating the forward six.

figures.title: Spread is measured from the mean, bias from the truth
figures.authoredReview: One estimate does not illustrate repeated sampling. Add an explicit four-outcome experiment with separate truth, mean, and spread.
figures.prediction: If all four estimates move together, does their spread around their own mean change?

individualReview.observation: Four gray outcomes surround their red mean, while the blue truth is offset by one unit; dotted spread links and the 1+2=3 decomposition remain distinct.

figures.title: Two perfect training fits disagree between observed points
figures.authoredReview: An error curve can become another memorized shape. Pin two continuous fits to the same observations and expose their unconstrained between-point disagreement.
figures.prediction: Do the three observed pins determine the prediction halfway between them?

individualReview.observation: Both curves meet all three observed pins and separate at the marked half-step; the title and caption now teach interpolation freedom rather than promising a universal descent curve.

figures.title: Averaging changes the mean's distribution, not the original observations
figures.authoredReview: Two densities omit averaging itself. Gather ten skewed observations into one mean while retaining the original source density.
figures.prediction: Does collecting means alter the distribution of an individual future observation?

individualReview.observation: Ten sampled points converge to one mean, while the original exponential population stays separate from the narrower exact distribution of means.

figures.title: Pooling collapses space while keeping one output per channel
figures.authoredReview: Shape tokens obscure the reduction axes. Collapse each actual spatial map into its own output while preserving channel color and identity.
figures.prediction: How many outputs remain when only the spatial axes are averaged?

individualReview.observation: Each colored 4x4 channel has its own divide-by-sixteen route and output; pooling preserves three channel identities rather than collapsing everything into one.

figures.title: Three observations reshape uncertainty; they do not prove a fixed success rate
figures.authoredReview: A final density hides evidence weighting. Keep the prior, show the three observations, and reshape the whole density rather than declaring a point estimate.
figures.prediction: Do three observations make every probability except 0.6 impossible?

individualReview.observation: Two successes and one failure reshape the uniform prior into a broad Beta(3,2) density, with the mean 0.6 shown without claiming certainty.

figures.title: Cross-entropy keeps a strong gradient for a confident wrong answer
figures.authoredReview: Wrong confidence and saturation are separate mechanisms. Compare the full BCE sensitivity with squared error passing through the small sigmoid gate.
figures.prediction: At predicted probability 0.01 for a positive label, which gradient remains large?

individualReview.observation: The near-full cross-entropy gradient bar contrasts with the tiny squared-error bar through the extra sigmoid slope, despite the same confidently wrong probability.

figures.title: The probability factors cancel; the input still scales the weight gradient
figures.authoredReview: Cancellation should leave a visible surviving route. Trace a concrete positive-label gradient through the sigmoid and then the input.
figures.prediction: If the input is zero, can the weight receive this nonzero logit gradient?

individualReview.observation: The probability-factor product yields the -0.8 logit gradient, then a separate input-times-three route yields the -2.4 weight gradient.

figures.title: Square-root scaling stabilizes variance only under the stated dependence assumptions
figures.authoredReview: Dividing a standard deviation scales both dimensions of its variance square. Keep sixty-four independent unit contributions visible before shrinking.
figures.prediction: Why does dividing the dot product by eight divide its variance by sixty-four?

individualReview.observation: An eight-by-eight variance square contracts to one tile; SD eight and variance sixty-four remain separate quantities under the stated independence assumption.

figures.title: Swapping columns reverses orientation without changing absolute area
figures.authoredReview: A filled polygon cannot explain sign. Trace both column orders around the same parallelogram.
figures.prediction: Does reversing the column order change the floor area?

individualReview.observation: Opposite edge traversal arrows enclose the same parallelogram, exposing determinant +4/-4 without changing the unsigned floor area.

figures.title: A straight-through backward rule is not the hard operation's derivative
figures.authoredReview: The hard forward gate stays unchanged when a surrogate reverse route is declared. Draw both directions separately and name the surrogate explicitly.
figures.prediction: Does choosing a straight-through gradient smooth the actual forward threshold?

individualReview.observation: The two displayed paths distinguish the discrete forward choice from its backward surrogate; neither picture presents the surrogate as the literal derivative of the sampling event.

figures.title: Scaling preserves expected activation, not every realized training pass
figures.authoredReview: Arithmetic does not distinguish a draw from its expectation. Branch one activation into two alternative realizations and reunite only their weighted average.
figures.prediction: Does one pass return the mean of the two branches?

individualReview.observation: Direct final inspection and native-font stroke clearance show both fifty-percent labels above the branches; actual outcomes zero/eight remain separate from expected four.

figures.title: Change coordinates, scale eigenvector components, then change coordinates back
figures.authoredReview: A token multiplication does not show independent axes. Stretch the actual coordinate displacements by different eigenvalues.
figures.prediction: Does scaling the first eigen-coordinate require mixing it with the second?

individualReview.observation: The eigenbasis decomposition and recombined vector preserve the separate coordinate contributions, while scaling acts on each basis direction instead of using one scalar for the whole input.

figures.title: Normalization removes the length advantage that made A win the raw dot product
figures.authoredReview: Ranking bars hide angle and length. Pull candidates onto a unit circle and compare their query-axis projections.
figures.prediction: After normalization, can increasing only A’s original length improve its cosine?

individualReview.observation: The diagonal vector meets the same unit-radius arc as the aligned vector; raw scores ten/one reverse to cosines .7071/one without changing direction.

figures.title: Fair marginals can still share 0.531 bits of information
figures.authoredReview: An information budget hides conditional dependence. Route fair input bits mostly straight through, with thin crossover paths for flips.
figures.prediction: If both outgoing paths became equally likely, would the input still predict the output?

individualReview.observation: Both marginals stay fifty-fifty, but thick retained-bit and thin flipped-bit paths expose the ninety/ten channel and the nonzero .531-bit information.

figures.title: Separated model means add uncertainty even when each model is confident
figures.authoredReview: Mean markers hide each model’s outcomes. Separate within-model displacement from movement between model centers.
figures.prediction: Can individually concentrated models form a wide mixture?

individualReview.observation: Two narrow pairs lie far apart around their separate model means; the mixture mean 2.5 is distinct from within .16 and between 2.25 contributions.

figures.title: A value at its mean contributes zero to covariance
figures.authoredReview: A sign table hides joint deviations. Put observations in the four centered quadrants and on the zero-contribution axis.
figures.prediction: Which sign changes if only the centered x deviation changes sign?

individualReview.observation: Equal-sign centered quadrants carry positive products, opposite-sign quadrants negative products, and the point on a centered axis contributes zero.

figures.title: A big error in a small bin can match a small error in a large bin
figures.authoredReview: Equal results hide different causes. Make bin share and gap orthogonal dimensions of equal contribution areas.
figures.prediction: What happens if only the first bin doubles in size?

individualReview.observation: Different weights and reliability gaps form equal four-percent rectangles on a shared area scale; the displayed sum is expressly the shown contributions, not unshown bins.

figures.title: Repeated small multipliers erase gradients; large ones amplify them
figures.authoredReview: Power curves conceal local repetition. Pass the same unit signal through ten identical gates and let its width compound.
figures.prediction: Is depth alone sufficient to say whether this signal grows?

individualReview.observation: Repeated local multipliers move the same reverse signal through successive depth positions, showing amplification or shrinkage rather than using the final norm as an unexplained label.

figures.title: Keep the success count and sample size; their ratio estimates the mean
figures.authoredReview: A sum ledger hides what is discarded. Permute the observed bits, then compress both orders into the same count pair.
figures.prediction: Can the Bernoulli likelihood distinguish these two orders under the stated independent model?

individualReview.observation: The three observations compress to count and sum, and the one-third fitted mean follows from those sufficient statistics without claiming recovery of the individual sample order.

figures.title: Shared factors explain covariance; independent noise adds only diagonal variance
figures.authoredReview: Off-diagonal dependence should be the same shared cause appearing in both assets. Build all four covariance products from one factor and distinguish independent diagonal noise.
figures.prediction: Can independent asset noise add an off-diagonal covariance term?

individualReview.observation: One shared-factor component connects both feature directions, while separately drawn residual components retain feature-specific variation rather than becoming a second common factor.

figures.title: Shared embeddings estimate an unseen pair without a dedicated pair weight
figures.authoredReview: An unseen pair should reuse matching coordinate products, not acquire a fictional observation. Collect the two shared embedding contributions.
figures.prediction: Does estimating the interaction prove that this feature pair was observed?

individualReview.observation: The unseen pair receives a score from existing shared feature embeddings, visibly distinguishing transferable parameters from a learned dedicated A/B lookup entry.

figures.title: A broader numeric range leaves fewer bits for nearby distinctions
figures.authoredReview: One format alone hides the tradeoff. Reassign three of the same sixteen physical bit slots from fraction to exponent.
figures.prediction: Can this fixed-size layout add exponent bits without taking them from another field?

individualReview.observation: The equal sixteen-slot envelopes preserve total width while moving exponent versus fraction ownership; the diagram distinguishes range from nearby-value resolution.
