figures.title: One point updates both components with weights summing to one
figures.authoredReview: A stacked percentage hides observation identity. Divide one unit of observation mass between two updates without duplicating it.
figures.prediction: If both branches received a full observation, how much total mass would be counted?

individualReview.observation: The same point sends fractional weight to both mixture components; prior-weighted density areas precede normalization, so responsibility is not determined by distance alone.

figures.title: Halving memory traffic raises this example's ceiling from 1 to 2 TFLOP/s
figures.authoredReview: Arithmetic intensity is work per transferred byte. Keep bandwidth fixed while each byte supports one or two work units, and label the result as a ceiling.
figures.prediction: Does a doubled memory ceiling prove an observed throughput doubled?

individualReview.observation: Equal byte routes create one versus two work tiles under the same one-TB/s assumption; the one/two-TFLOP/s labels explicitly describe ceilings, not measured speed.

figures.title: Four backwards add gradients while the parameters remain fixed
figures.authoredReview: Four passes should carry the same parameter version until the accumulated gradient crosses one optimizer boundary.
figures.prediction: Which microbatch in this accumulation cycle sees parameter version v1?

individualReview.observation: All four backward contributions retain parameter v0 while their fan-in reaches ten; only the separate optimizer boundary creates v1.

figures.title: Fit the remaining errors, not the original targets again
figures.authoredReview: A ledger obscures distance. Put prediction and target on one ruler, then move only one tenth of the residual.
figures.prediction: Does the new tree add the full target or a fraction of what remains?

individualReview.observation: The same target-ten endpoint is preserved as prediction seven moves to 7.3; residual three is multiplied by .1 instead of re-adding the target.

figures.title: Shorten the whole gradient vector without changing its direction
figures.authoredReview: Two vectors do not expose the constraint. Add the norm boundary and pull the original point inward along its existing ray.
figures.prediction: Does clipping rotate this gradient toward an axis?

individualReview.observation: The original and clipped points share one ray, with actual radii five/two and coordinates (3,4)/(1.2,1.6), so clipping visibly preserves direction.

figures.title: Only B and its neighbours contribute to B's current update
figures.authoredReview: One node update gathers only its declared neighborhood. Add an isolated counterexample whose large feature must not leak into the aggregation.
figures.prediction: Can the isolated node’s value enter B without an edge?

individualReview.observation: A and C have live routes into B's update, while the isolated D=100 hypothetical route is crossed out and excluded from the mean two.

figures.title: A probability of 0.8 does not pick an action without its costs
figures.authoredReview: A probability is not an action. Show error probability multiplying error cost and choose between the resulting areas.
figures.prediction: Would the same score choose the same action if false-positive cost fell to one?

individualReview.observation: Different error widths and cost heights yield areas two versus .8; the negative action wins by expected cost despite the shared positive probability .8.

figures.title: Equal logit steps multiply odds rather than add fixed probability
figures.authoredReview: Three number rows hide spacing. Connect the same candidates through equally spaced logits, multiplicative odds, and compressed probabilities.
figures.prediction: Does another unit logit step add the same probability near the upper end?

individualReview.observation: Equal logit spacing links to multiplicative odds and a compressed probability ruler; the upper-end probability increments visibly shrink rather than staying additive.

figures.title: The kernel reaches 36 without constructing either feature vector
figures.authoredReview: The shortcut must end at the same quantity. Count thirty-six unit contributions through explicit features and through the compact square.
figures.prediction: Does the compact route approximate the expanded feature result?

individualReview.observation: The explicit feature-product grids total thirty-six units and the compact six-by-six grid encloses the same area, supporting exact equality rather than approximation.

figures.title: Changing which distribution does the averaging reverses this candidate ranking
figures.authoredReview: The averaging distribution should be physically different. Keep P fixed in forward comparisons, then draw each candidate’s different population in reverse comparisons.
figures.prediction: Which distribution supplies the averaging weights in reverse KL?

individualReview.observation: The two forward panels retain P's same averaging cohort, while reverse panels use each candidate cohort; common-width KL bars expose the genuine ranking reversal.

figures.title: Uniform mixing leaves target mass 0.92, not 0.90
figures.authoredReview: A two-part bar hides where the uniform mass goes. Spread ten of one hundred target units across all five classes, including the true one.
figures.prediction: Does the true class also receive its share of the uniform mass?

individualReview.observation: The true class retains ninety original units plus its own two uniform units; the other four classes each receive two, preserving one hundred total units.

figures.title: A nonzero decay floor shifts the midpoint above half the peak
figures.authoredReview: Separate the persistent floor from the decaying headroom. The midpoint retains half of the 0.8 headroom, not half of the total one.
figures.prediction: Why is the post-warmup midpoint 0.6 rather than 0.5?

individualReview.observation: The fixed .2 floor remains beneath every checkpoint, while only the .8 headroom halves at midpoint to produce .6 rather than .5.

figures.title: The residual is perpendicular to the fitted column space
figures.authoredReview: A right-angle symbol states optimality without demonstrating it. Add a feasible rail and a longer competing fit-to-observation tether.
figures.prediction: Can another coefficient representation change the same projected prediction?

individualReview.observation: The shortest observation tether meets the feasible prediction rail at a right angle; the longer competing tether distinguishes projection optimality from unique coefficient representation.

figures.title: Forget and input gates scale separate contributions before they add
figures.authoredReview: The two gates are independent valves, not a normalized mixture. Preserve the old-state and candidate contributions until they merge.
figures.prediction: If the input gate closes, which contribution remains?

individualReview.observation: Separate old-state and candidate routes retain their .8 and .5 gates until the 1.6 and 1.5 contributions join into 3.1; the gates are not normalized mixture weights.

figures.title: Balanced probability flow preserves the distribution while transitions continue
figures.authoredReview: Transition rates differ because reservoir masses differ. Draw unequal stationary stores with equal opposite mass flows.
figures.prediction: Can the stationary distribution stay fixed while individual states continue moving?

individualReview.observation: Unequal stationary reservoirs have equal opposite 2/15 mass flows, keeping distribution balance distinct from unchanged individual states or equal transition probabilities.

figures.title: A nonzero input can collapse to zero when matrix columns are dependent
figures.authoredReview: Origin vectors obscure head-to-tail cancellation. Send one nonzero contribution out and the other back to the origin.
figures.prediction: Can a nonzero coefficient vector disappear under dependent columns?

individualReview.observation: The nonzero outgoing column contribution is followed by its cancelling return to the origin, making disappearance under dependent columns a geometric action rather than a zero-input claim.

figures.title: Each parameter receives contributions from every output it influences
figures.authoredReview: Each input column collects from every output. Give local derivatives height and upstream output sensitivities width before gathering each column.
figures.prediction: Which input loses a contribution if only one output row is propagated?

individualReview.observation: Each input column gathers both output sensitivities through separately weighted areas, yielding five and eight without dropping an output's contribution.

figures.title: Matching user and item coordinates multiply, then sum to the missing rating
figures.authoredReview: Keep the missing rating distinct from a recorded value. Gather aligned user-item coordinate products into an explicitly estimated result.
figures.prediction: Which observation would be required to call five a recorded rating?

individualReview.observation: Aligned user/item coordinate products three and two join at an explicitly estimated five; the missing observation remains distinct from the prediction.

figures.title: Hold the observations fixed while comparing candidate probabilities
figures.authoredReview: A final peak hides what is held fixed. Pass the same five outcomes through three candidate probabilities and multiply their evidence factors.
figures.prediction: Why do the two failures penalize the 0.9 candidate?

individualReview.observation: The same three successes and two failures feed all candidate probabilities; the failures visibly penalize .9, so the comparison does not change its observed sample.

figures.title: Average branch returns by their probabilities rather than choosing the best outcome
figures.authoredReview: The best leaf is not the chance-node answer. Make both return contributions occupy countable probability-times-return areas.
figures.prediction: Can the value become two while the lower-return branch still has positive probability?

individualReview.observation: The two branch areas contribute 1.5 and .25 to 1.75; the chance-node result gathers both instead of selecting the best possible return two.

figures.title: Five draws remain five draws even when unequal weights yield ESS 2.5
figures.authoredReview: Repeated weight is easily mistaken for repeated evidence. Keep exactly five observation identities while enlarging their influence areas.
figures.prediction: Does enlarging the first draw create another independent observation?

individualReview.observation: Five separately numbered observations retain five source identities even though their weights become six/one/one/one/one; the larger first weight yields ESS 2.5 without creating draws.

figures.title: Equal gradient lengths do not resolve opposing directions
figures.authoredReview: Equal norm markers must preserve direction. Join the unit vectors head-to-tail so their cancellation is visible.
figures.prediction: Does matching the two norms resolve their opposing update directions?

individualReview.observation: Equal-length rightward and leftward arrows return to the same origin and sum to zero, making directional cancellation distinct from matched unit norms.

figures.title: Multiplying evidence ratios requires conditional independence within each class
figures.authoredReview: Preserve the comparison class while independent evidence doubles the other class weight twice.
figures.prediction: What assumption permits the second likelihood ratio to multiply the first?

individualReview.observation: The same relative-weight strip changes from one-to-four to two-to-four to four-to-four, exposing twenty, 33.33, and fifty percent under explicitly independent likelihood ratios.

figures.title: At fixed compute, more parameters leave fewer training tokens
figures.authoredReview: A hyperbola hides the conserved resource. Reshape the same eight compute tiles by exchanging parameter and token axes.
figures.prediction: Can both dimensions double while these eight tiles stay fixed?

individualReview.observation: The two-by-four and four-by-two rectangles both contain eight equal compute tiles; doubling parameter width halves token height without an optimality or speed measurement claim.

figures.title: Expanding volume lowers density while preserving probability mass
figures.authoredReview: Trace four persistent probability marks through a doubled domain. Expand space without multiplying observations or mass.

individualReview.observation: All four quarter-mass dots remain inside the expanded enclosure; doubling area lowers the stated density from one to .5 without changing total mass one.

figures.title: Bits per token cannot compare models fairly when token units differ
figures.authoredReview: The same text occupies different numbers of token buckets. Hold total code length fixed and contrast per-token and per-character denominators.
figures.prediction: Can equal total code length yield different perplexities under different tokenizations?

individualReview.observation: The same a/b/c/d characters occupy four individual or two paired token boxes; four total bits yield perplexities two/four while bits per character stays one.

figures.title: A positive return still suppresses an action when it falls below baseline
figures.authoredReview: A negative bar is a memorized sign. Measure the actual return backward from the baseline on the same ruler.
figures.prediction: Can a positive raw return still discourage the sampled action?

individualReview.observation: Return three is positive but lies left of baseline five on the same ruler; the backward two-unit arrow gives negative advantage rather than encouraging the action from raw return alone.

figures.title: Importance weights change estimated contribution, not the observed click count
figures.authoredReview: Keep one observed click visibly singular while its inverse-examination contribution expands to five units.

individualReview.observation: One numbered click maps to a larger weight-five circle under examination .2; the source still contains one observation rather than five clicks.

figures.title: A zero-curvature direction lets a quadratic sublevel set extend without bound
figures.authoredReview: A flat line should be an escape route in parameter space. Draw the zero-loss center of an indefinitely extending sublevel strip.

individualReview.observation: The zero-curvature valley extends in both y directions while remaining inside the same x-squared sublevel strip; points at x zero can move without raising loss.

figures.title: High precision cannot hide low recall in the harmonic mean
figures.authoredReview: Show the reciprocal cost hidden in the harmonic mean. A weak rate creates a large contribution to the reciprocal denominator.

individualReview.observation: The recall reciprocal-ten rectangle dominates the precision reciprocal-1.111 rectangle on one scale, exposing harmonic F1 .18 rather than arithmetic average .5.

figures.title: Counting events and waiting for the next event require different random variables
figures.authoredReview: Use one event stream to define two different observations: count marks in a fixed window, or measure the gap to the next event.

individualReview.observation: The same three event marks support a count-three observation and a separate 1.42-second inter-event gap; the waiting-time arrow measures continuous duration, not fractional event count.

figures.title: In this model, correlated tree variation leaves a nonzero variance floor
figures.authoredReview: Correlated error is a retained common component. Average away private variance while keeping the same common tiles in every ensemble.
figures.prediction: Which component remains even as the number of trees becomes very large?

individualReview.observation: The four red shared-error tiles persist while blue private-error tiles shrink across one/four/sixteen trees, leaving the explicit .2 variance floor in the stated model.

individualReview.observation: Upstream 2.2 is copied to both branches before their separate one/.1 derivatives produce 2.2/.22 and sum 2.42; addition does not halve the identity-branch gradient.

figures.title: Potential differences cancel this undiscounted loop; entry bonuses accumulate
figures.authoredReview: Show the return trip undoing the same potential gain. A closed physical loop makes the cancellation memorable.
figures.prediction: Can cycling between these two states accumulate undiscounted potential reward?

individualReview.observation: The outbound two-to-five potential gain three is repaid by minus three on return to the same potential-two state, leaving zero undiscounted loop reward.

figures.title: Keep the coordinate along PC1; discard the perpendicular reconstruction error
figures.authoredReview: Make the retained line a physical constraint. Drop the observation onto it and retain the discarded perpendicular tether.

individualReview.observation: The observation three/two projects to three/zero on the green first-component rail; the perpendicular two-unit tether is discarded reconstruction error, not a second retained coordinate.

figures.title: Repeated matches saturate while extra document length can reduce their score
figures.authoredReview: Term frequency and length must describe actual documents. Preserve four highlighted matches while adding nonmatching words, then compare eight matches at the original length.
figures.prediction: Do extra nonmatching words improve the same four-match score?

individualReview.observation: Four highlighted matches stay fixed as extra nonmatching words lower the factor from 1.692 to 1.443; eight matches at the original length reach 1.913 rather than doubling the score.

figures.title: Under these assumptions, variance 2/fan-in preserves the ReLU second moment
figures.authoredReview: Initialization is a repeated moment multiplier, not a promise of universal stability. Carry the second moment through ten layers.
figures.prediction: Can repeatedly losing half the second moment preserve its initial scale?

individualReview.observation: Ten successive half-moment gates shrink one to .0009766, while the compensated unit-gain lane preserves one under the explicitly stated moment assumptions, not a universal stability guarantee.

figures.title: A shared logit shift leaves probabilities unchanged but changes z-loss
figures.authoredReview: A common offset expands every unnormalized mass by the same factor. Renormalize both into identical shares while their log-normalizers remain different.
figures.prediction: Which quantity changes even when every softmax probability stays fixed?

individualReview.observation: The common logit shift changes log-normalizer 1.313 to 3.313 while both normalized strips retain .269/.731; probability invariance does not erase the offset measured by z-loss.

figures.title: Four-layer segments balance saved and rebuilt states in this model
figures.authoredReview: A minimum curve hides competing inventories. Count saved segment boundaries and the currently rebuilt segment on separate physical rails.
figures.prediction: Why does saving fewer boundaries eventually require more concurrent rebuilt states?

individualReview.observation: Saved boundary dots and rebuilt squares change in opposite directions; the four-layer case visibly balances 4+4 against 16+1 and 2+8.

figures.title: Stop the advantage gradient; keep both losses updating shared features
figures.authoredReview: Differentiate shared features from the detached advantage target. Show both head gradients reaching the trunk while the actor-to-advantage route stops.
figures.prediction: Does stopping the advantage route also stop the actor from updating shared features?

individualReview.observation: The repaired stopped-advantage route travels around the shared node, not through its label; both solid head-to-trunk gradient routes remain unobstructed.

figures.title: One backward scan adds the same decaying residuals
figures.authoredReview: The weighted sum hides its time direction. Pull the future accumulator backward, decay it, then add the current residual.
figures.prediction: Which residual crosses two decay boundaries before reaching the first time step?

individualReview.observation: The backward vertical decay links connect -1 to 1.2 to 1.96, and each horizontal residual addition is readable next to its own step.

figures.title: BatchNorm shares statistics across samples; LayerNorm keeps each token separate
figures.authoredReview: The mean table hides the pooling axis. Encircle rows and then columns of the same four values before computing the two different summaries.
figures.prediction: Would exchanging the two samples change which features share a BatchNorm mean?

individualReview.observation: The same 2x2 values switch between row and column grouping, exposing LayerNorm means 2/6 versus BatchNorm means 3/5.

figures.title: New samples move confidence intervals; a posterior conditions on this sample
figures.authoredReview: Keep truth fixed while repeated intervals move, then keep one dataset fixed while posterior uncertainty spans possible parameters.
figures.prediction: Which panel repeats the data, and which conditions on one observed dataset?

individualReview.observation: The repeated-interval panel moves around one fixed truth; the separate Beta(4,3) panel conditions on one observed sample and is explicitly not a coverage experiment.

figures.title: Sum over the hidden branch, then normalize the combined evidence
figures.authoredReview: Show marginalization as gathering both weighted hidden-state contributions, rather than choosing a hidden state.
figures.prediction: What contribution disappears if the second hidden state is wrongly discarded?

individualReview.observation: Weighted rectangle areas 0.6 and 0.35 become a shared 0.95 message; later normalization is explicitly separate from this hidden-state sum.

figures.title: 15% are prediction targets; only some of those targets become masks
figures.authoredReview: Target membership and visible replacement are different sets. Keep token identities through selection and show unchanged targets inside the selected group.
figures.prediction: Can an unchanged visible token still contribute a prediction loss?

individualReview.observation: The same selected positions remain targets after their colors change into 120 masked, 15 random, and 15 unchanged tokens; unchanged visibility does not erase selection.

figures.title: Resample users with all their paired events, not isolated rows
figures.authoredReview: User identities must carry their paired events. Duplicate an entire selected user cluster, not unrelated event rows.
figures.prediction: Which events travel together when user A is sampled twice?

individualReview.observation: The A/C/A sample repeats both a1 and a2 together, preserving cluster identity and showing B absent rather than duplicating independent rows.

figures.title: Detaching keeps the hidden value but cuts earlier gradient paths
figures.authoredReview: A table cannot distinguish forward transport from reverse sensitivity. Let the hidden value cross a wall while the returning gradient stops.
figures.prediction: Does stopping the gradient reset the hidden value to zero?

individualReview.observation: The boundary now has a clear gap around the unchanged-value sentence; the forward h=2 crosses while the reverse gradient ends at the stop marker.

figures.title: A shared cause can link messages and churn without a treatment effect
figures.authoredReview: Association is a surviving common-cause route. Compare observational assignment with an intervention that cuts the assignment edge without changing the outcome edge.

individualReview.observation: The observed common cause reaches both messages and churn; the intervention removes only the assignment edge into messages, keeping the other causal route intact.

figures.title: Transition scores can overturn the locally best labels
figures.authoredReview: The transition penalty is backward motion from the accumulated emission score. Follow complete paths rather than choosing each emission independently.
figures.prediction: Does the path with the best local emissions still win after its transition penalty?

individualReview.observation: AA's emission score moves left by its negative transition cost to -1, while AB stays at three and BB at two on shared horizontal rulers.

figures.title: A blank separates repeated letters so both survive CTC collapse
figures.authoredReview: The blank is a separator before it is deleted. Track the two surviving a identities across both ordered transformations.
figures.prediction: Would deleting the blank before merging leave the same number of a outputs?

individualReview.observation: Consecutive a emissions share the same identity color and merge before blank removal; the separated final a survives, leaving the two-symbol output aa.

figures.title: Shared content features let an unseen item match a user's interests
figures.authoredReview: A dot-product ledger hides feature alignment. Give the two aligned coordinate products their own equal-scale areas.
figures.prediction: Can swapping the item coordinates change the match score?

individualReview.observation: Interest widths and item-feature heights produce two and three area contributions, allowing an unseen item to receive the displayed content score five.

figures.title: Rotate key/value blocks; merge their normalization, not separately normalized answers
figures.authoredReview: Equal local averages obscure unequal evidence. Weight each local answer by its share of the combined normalizer.
figures.prediction: Why is the answer not the equal average six?

individualReview.observation: The local values two and ten receive weights 0.2/0.8 from unequal normalizers; shared tiles expose the correct 8.4 instead of an equal average six.

figures.title: The declared positive enters the denominator; an undeclared positive remains a negative
figures.authoredReview: Carry the declared positive identity into its own denominator alongside both negative candidates. Semantic relevance cannot silently change the declared labels.
figures.prediction: Is the declared positive excluded from the denominator candidate set?

individualReview.observation: The relocated denominator heading clears the persistent positive-identity route; the same positive enters both sets while N1/N2 remain declared negatives.

figures.title: Each local patch becomes one column in the matrix product
figures.authoredReview: The matrix alone hides overlap. Select two neighboring patches from one image and preserve each pixel identity in the resulting columns.

individualReview.observation: Two overlapping 2x2 enclosures map to separate columns, visibly repeating the same middle pixels two and five rather than inventing independent pixels.

figures.title: Top-k fixes a count; top-p changes the count to reach a probability mass
figures.authoredReview: A stacked mass bar does not expose membership. Keep one hundred probability units and select the same token identities under two different rules.

individualReview.observation: Fixed top-two selection retains mass .70, while the .80 probability threshold includes the third token and reaches .85 without relabeling token identities.

figures.title: Train at one sampled noise level; generate through a dependent chain
figures.authoredReview: A training example samples one time; generation requires the predecessor result. Compare an independent sampled-time loss with a dependent reverse chain.
figures.prediction: Can the second reverse transition run without the first transition’s output?

individualReview.observation: Training chooses one noise-time position, whereas the separate z3/z2/z1/x0 generation chain has explicit predecessor-dependent arrows.

figures.title: The same input distribution can hide a different label rule
figures.authoredReview: Input matching is insufficient when labels flip. Keep the same four input identities while changing only their class colors.
figures.prediction: Can a method checking only the input counts detect this reversed rule?

individualReview.observation: The source/target conditional distributions are separately represented, making the covariate-shift assumption explicit instead of treating every target change as reweightable.

figures.title: Raise a touching lower bound to prevent the likelihood from falling
figures.authoredReview: A pair of curves can hide the monotonicity mechanism. Mark their contact, climb the supporting bound, and then read the higher true objective.
figures.prediction: Why is the true objective at the new bound maximum no lower than the old objective?

individualReview.observation: The bound contacts the current likelihood before its own ascent step; contact and upward motion are distinct, with no automatic promise of a global maximum.

figures.title: One reverse sweep computes all parameter gradients for this scalar loss
figures.authoredReview: One scalar objective should initiate one reverse flow. Follow a shared sensitivity into two parameter derivatives rather than restarting from the loss.
figures.prediction: Does each parameter require a separate complete reverse traversal?

individualReview.observation: One loss emits a common upstream derivative, then branches toward differently weighted parameter sensitivities; the final gradient values are not copies of one forward output.

figures.title: An uncertainty bonus or a posterior draw can overturn the mean leader
figures.authoredReview: The decision must reflect the operation applied to each same arm. Compare mean locations, uncertainty bonuses, and one posterior draw on common rulers.
figures.prediction: Can the lower estimated mean win an uncertainty-aware choice?

individualReview.observation: Exploration, optimistic selection, and sampled uncertainty are represented as different choice mechanisms over the same alternatives, rather than interchangeable reward bars.

figures.title: Conditioning narrows uncertainty where observed points are informative
figures.authoredReview: A single standard-deviation curve hides the constrained prediction envelope. Pin the whole symmetric band at the observed input and let it reopen with distance.
figures.prediction: Does one noiseless observation eliminate uncertainty everywhere?

individualReview.observation: A new observed point locally constrains the posterior and narrows nearby uncertainty; the remaining unsampled regions are not flattened into equal certainty.

figures.title: Conditioning can close a chain while opening a collider
figures.authoredReview: A truth table hides the graph motif. Draw chain and collider directions before marking how observing their middle changes connectivity.

individualReview.observation: The chain's observed middle closes its path, whereas the collider's observed middle opens its path; arrow directions and middle-state colors remain explicit.

figures.title: Share key/value pairs without merging the eight query outputs

individualReview.observation: Two stored KV boxes each feed four separately numbered query/output routes, visibly preserving eight independent output identities despite shared storage.

figures.title: A zero adapter output can still give B a nonzero first gradient
figures.authoredReview: A zero output does not sever every sensitivity route. Compare the factor that vanishes in each initial derivative.
figures.prediction: Which factor has a nonzero first gradient despite the zero adapter output?

figures.title: Add both contributions at the shared node before propagating its gradient

individualReview.observation: Twelve and two first join into fourteen at the shared node, then the common times-three route yields forty-two; propagation cannot omit the second contribution.

figures.title: Add confusion counts across shards before computing the combined F1

figures.prediction: Why does the one-case shard not receive half the pooled denominator?

figures.title: Fix assignments before moving each centroid to its assigned mean
figures.authoredReview: Move each center to the balance point of its assigned observations, while keeping the assignment colors fixed.
figures.prediction: During this centroid update, can a point silently change its assigned cluster?

individualReview.observation: Points zero/two remain in the left assigned group and eight/ten in the right; each centroid arrow reaches its own fixed-assignment mean one/nine.

figures.title: Higher temperature exposes alternatives without changing the winning class
figures.authoredReview: A rounded table does not expose redistributed probability. Recompute exact softmax masses and transfer width from the winner to both alternatives.

individualReview.observation: Both full-width probability strips preserve class order, while temperature two transfers visible mass from winning A into the two losing classes B/C.

figures.title: Complex conjugation lets the reversed relation receive a different score
figures.authoredReview: A sign ledger does not reveal the orientation change. Multiply unit complex factors as quarter-turns and expose the real-axis endpoint after swapping.
figures.prediction: Why does conjugating the swapped head reverse the rotation?

individualReview.observation: The forward and swapped complex products point to opposite real-axis endpoints -1/+1 on equal circles, exposing antisymmetry from the conjugated swapped head.

figures.title: An L1 corner can touch the loss at an exactly zero coefficient
figures.authoredReview: Endpoints alone do not show why one coordinate disappears. Project the same target onto an actual diamond and circle with equal geometric scales.
figures.prediction: Which boundary has a corner on a coordinate axis?

individualReview.observation: The same target projects onto an actual axis corner of the diamond versus a smooth circle boundary, leaving an exactly zero second coordinate only in the L1 example.

figures.title: The same pair error matters more when its swap changes NDCG more
figures.authoredReview: A bar comparison hides rank location. Move the same relevant item through two equal-distance swaps on a fixed discount ladder.

individualReview.observation: One-rank displacements occupy different parts of the same discount ladder; the top swap has a visibly larger impact than the nine-to-ten swap.

figures.title: The likeliest state at one time need not belong to the likeliest path
figures.authoredReview: Separate most-probable marginals can imply a most-probable path. Show the four complete-path masses and pool them along each time axis.
figures.prediction: Is the path AB formed by the marginal winners the largest single path?

individualReview.observation: Path-mass combination and best-path choice have separately directed traces, preventing a sum over alternatives from being read as one maximizing hidden sequence.

figures.title: Hidden states connect observations that have no direct edge
figures.authoredReview: Keep the horizontal dependency in the hidden state lane and make every observed emission a local vertical child.
figures.prediction: Does a direct arrow between neighboring observations belong in this HMM?

individualReview.observation: Only the hidden lane has temporal arrows, and each observation has its own downward parent route; no direct observation-to-observation edge is fabricated.

figures.title: Choose the useful descent region, not the unstable end of the sweep
figures.authoredReview: A sweep curve hides the local stability mechanism. Run three update gains from the same quadratic coordinate and show contraction, oscillation, or growth.

individualReview.observation: The same zero reference separates contraction, contracting oscillation, and growing oscillation under coordinate multipliers .8, -.8, and -1.2.

figures.title: The mask zeroes future weight before the weighted value sum
figures.authoredReview: Zeros in a row look like ordinary small weights. Put an explicit time barrier before future positions and stop their contribution routes.
figures.prediction: Can a future key contribute a tiny positive amount through this mask?

individualReview.observation: Query position two has three live weights .2/.3/.5; positions three/four stop at the barrier and receive exactly zero, not tiny soft contributions.

figures.title: A candidate below the running top two cannot re-enter later

figures.prediction: Why is previously discarded three unnecessary when eight arrives?

figures.title: Reuse old key/value projections; compute only the newest query row
figures.authoredReview: The access row should remain intact even when old projections are reused. Draw three stored keys and one newly written key under the single new query.

individualReview.observation: The new Q3 fans to all four KV objects, with only KV3 newly appended; retaining old projections does not remove their attention-access routes.

figures.title: Normalize each learned branch without replacing the identity stream
figures.authoredReview: The normalized branch must not replace the raw stream. Carry one unchanged input along a bypass and add the learned correction at the end.

figures.title: Write one new pair while reading the growing cache
figures.authoredReview: Different-height bars hide cache identity. Preserve seven old pairs, append the eighth, and visibly read all eight.

individualReview.observation: Direct repaired-image inspection shows all eight KV objects on one row with unobstructed query routes; seven retained objects remain distinct from the single newly written eighth.

figures.authoredReview: The kernel route stores sufficient feature sums before queries arrive. Work one exact positive-feature example, while retaining the distinct position-compression route in the derivation.

individualReview.observation: The positive-feature example gathers reusable numerator twenty-eight and normalizer six before its query read, without presenting it as exact softmax or conflating position compression.

figures.title: Scaling can preserve a small gradient before rounding destroys it

individualReview.observation: The upper rounding boundary sends two-to-minus-thirty to zero, while scaling first preserves two-to-minus-ten before explicit unscaling; later multiplication cannot restore already rounded information.

figures.title: The realized patch area determines the mixed target weights

figures.title: Average marginal credit across orderings, including repeated predecessor sets
figures.authoredReview: Abstract formulas hide the order-dependent marginal. Let the same total payoff be allocated in both feature orders, then average each feature’s two gains.
figures.prediction: Can choosing only one feature order give a different attribution?

individualReview.observation: Two entry-order strips keep the same payoff six but allocate two/four versus five/one; the averaged strip shows 3.5/2.5 rather than selecting one ordering.

figures.title: Split features into heads; every head still sees all tokens
figures.authoredReview: Splitting boxes can accidentally split time. Cut the feature columns while keeping every token row in each head, then reassemble them.
figures.prediction: Which head loses access to token two after this feature split?

individualReview.observation: All three token rows survive in both two-column heads and in the reconstructed four-column grid; only feature columns split, not token access.

figures.title: RoPE rotates vectors; ALiBi subtracts distance from attention scores
figures.authoredReview: Position can change coordinates before a dot product or change the score afterward. Draw the two routes with different entry points.
figures.prediction: Does an ALiBi penalty rotate the stored query and key vectors?

individualReview.observation: RoPE acts on both query/key coordinates before the dot product, while ALiBi's zero/-.5/-1 penalties belong to the score stage rather than rotating stored vectors.

figures.title: Clipping removes incentive in one direction; it does not bound the new policy ratio
figures.authoredReview: A clipped objective is not a ratio wall. Put an actual ratio outside the clipping interval on a flat objective segment.
figures.prediction: Is the ratio forbidden from reaching 1.6 when its objective contribution plateaus?

individualReview.observation: The positive-advantage plateau contains the marked ratio 1.6 beyond 1.2, and the negative plateau contains .6 below .8; objective flattening does not impose ratio containment.

figures.title: Zero weights leave dense shapes unchanged; removing channels shrinks them
figures.authoredReview: Count physical matrix slots before and after removal. Zeroing values keeps nine slots; deleting a row leaves six.
figures.prediction: Does filling a channel with zeros change the dense matrix shape?

individualReview.observation: The zero-filled middle channel still occupies a three-by-three grid until its row is structurally removed; only then do nine physical slots become six.

figures.title: The backup uses the best next action, not the action behavior sampled
figures.authoredReview: The behavior and backup choices should be different operations. Keep the sampled value two visible while the maximizing target route selects five.
figures.prediction: Does the backup use the behavior action simply because it was sampled?

individualReview.observation: The max gate chooses five from two/five, then discount .9 and reward one produce 5.5; the behavior action valued at two is not reused as the backup selection.

figures.title: One outlier can erase small values under a shared quantization scale
figures.authoredReview: The outlier changes representable spacing, not the original small values. Snap the same two signs onto coarse and fine rulers.
figures.prediction: Can the coarse shared scale distinguish these two small signs?

individualReview.observation: Opposite small signs both snap to code zero under shared scale two, while their own scale preserves -127/+127; the zoomed ruler isolates the outlier-induced resolution loss.

figures.title: Average precision accumulates relevant hits; reciprocal rank stops at the first
figures.authoredReview: Equal final values hide different collection rules. Follow the same relevance identities and show one metric stopping at the first hit.
figures.prediction: Which metric can change if a later relevant item moves?

individualReview.observation: The relevant hits at ranks two/four have separate one-half/two-fourths routes; RR stops at the first while AP gathers both, even though both equal .5 here.

figures.title: Hold the random draw fixed while gradients pass through its parameterized transformation
figures.authoredReview: The noise must remain external while the transformation moves. Pin one epsilon draw and move only the location parameter on the output ruler.
figures.prediction: Is another noise sample needed to differentiate this one transformation?

individualReview.observation: The noise circle remains minus one across both mean settings, moving the sample from 1.5 to 2.5 at fixed .5 scale without drawing another random value.

figures.title: Project the shortcut when spatial size or channel count changes
figures.authoredReview: Addition should be physically blocked by mismatched axes. Compare unmatched spatial/channel inventories with the projected shortcut that exactly matches the branch.
figures.prediction: Does matching only the spatial dimensions make this residual addition valid?

individualReview.observation: Height/width/channel comparisons all fail for eight/eight/sixteen versus four/four/thirty-two, then all match after projection; spatial agreement alone is not enough.

figures.title: Equal rewards give no within-group preference, even when every output passes
figures.authoredReview: Success markers alone imply useful preference. Subtract the shared group level from each equally rewarded output and show every residual vanish.
figures.prediction: Which output receives a positive centered preference when all rewards equal one?

individualReview.observation: Direct replacement inspection shows all four minus-one labels beside their arrows; reward-one outputs center to zero and supply no within-group preference.

figures.title: Blank edges advance time; token edges advance the output sequence
figures.authoredReview: Replace the state table with a traversable lattice. Two token moves share one time coordinate before blank moves advance audio time.
figures.prediction: Does emitting a second token require advancing to another audio frame?

individualReview.observation: Two horizontal token transitions preserve the audio row, while vertical blank transitions advance time; multiple output tokens do not require new audio frames.

figures.title: Rare positives let a small false-positive rate overwhelm true positives
figures.authoredReview: The rare-positive denominator must remain countable. Reuse the same nine hit identities in ten actual positives and 108 predicted positives.
figures.prediction: Why can an approximately one-percent false-positive rate still give low precision?

individualReview.observation: The same nine hit identities occupy ten actual positives and 108 predicted positives, making .9 recall coexist with nine-over-108 precision and ninety-nine false alarms.

figures.title: A shared position shift preserves the relative rotary angle, not every model output
figures.authoredReview: Rotate both actual direction arrows together and retain their right angle. A shared rotation preserves their dot product, not every model output.
figures.prediction: Does the ninety-degree angle change when both arrows rotate forty-five degrees?

individualReview.observation: The orthogonal arrows turn together by forty-five degrees and keep their ninety-degree separation; the caption limits invariance to this rotary interaction, not all model outputs.

figures.title: Queries determine output rows even when keys and values come from another sequence
figures.authoredReview: Route three source values into each of two distinct query destinations. Output count follows the destination query rows.
figures.prediction: Do three source keys create a third output when there are only two queries?

individualReview.observation: All three source key/value positions feed only two query circles, whose separate downward routes create exactly two output rows, not a third output from source count.

figures.title: Enlarging a coarse grid cannot recover an edge location that downsampling lost
figures.authoredReview: Pool two different boundary patterns into the same coarse value. Enlarge that one value and show the original distinction cannot be recovered.
figures.prediction: Which original pattern can be recovered from the coarse value alone?

individualReview.observation: Two distinct four-cell boundaries collapse to the same .5 coarse cell, exposing why enlargement cannot identify which fine-resolution pattern was pooled.

figures.title: Earlier physical position does not grant attention across example boundaries
figures.authoredReview: Earlier physical position is insufficient authority to attend. Draw two causal blocks and a sealed cross-example boundary.
figures.prediction: Can B1 read A1 merely because A1 appears earlier in the packed buffer?

individualReview.observation: Two triangular within-example blocks remain separated by the red boundary; later B tokens cannot read earlier A merely because its packed addresses precede them.

figures.title: In this recurrence, momentum reinforces persistent motion and damps alternating motion
figures.authoredReview: Persistent and alternating directions should drive the same recurrence. Track each retained velocity before adding the new gradient.
figures.prediction: Which sequence keeps reinforcing the same direction under beta 0.5?

individualReview.observation: Direct replacement inspection shows velocity arrows clear of both headings; persistent one/1.5/1.75/1.875 reinforces, while alternating one/-.5/.75/-.625 repeatedly reverses direction.

figures.title: Adding diagonal blocks cannot create cross-block products that were never computed
figures.authoredReview: Make all four required block slots physical. Fill only diagonal products and leave cross terms empty rather than pretending addition creates them.
figures.prediction: Can adding the two diagonal products create A0B1?

individualReview.observation: The blue diagonal products remain separate from red missing A0B1/A1B0 slots; adding available blocks cannot fill cross-products that were never computed.

figures.title: Gradient descent subtracts the gradient, raising the underpredicted true-class logit
figures.authoredReview: Negative sensitivity should move the true logit upward under descent. Draw actual before-and-after coordinates for all three logits.
figures.prediction: Why does a negative gradient raise the true-class logit?

individualReview.observation: Subtracting the true-class negative gradient moves its logit right to .2, while the positive one-third gradients move the other two left to -.1.

figures.title: An indirect global-token relay needs two layers to carry information
figures.authoredReview: One missing direct entry remains missing in one layer. Track B information into G, then into A on the next layer.
figures.prediction: Can A obtain B’s information through G in the first layer?

individualReview.observation: B information reaches G in the first layer while A stays untouched; only the second layer passes it to A, distinguishing adjacency from two-hop reach.

figures.title: Moving one threshold exchanges false rejections for false acceptances
figures.authoredReview: Move a threshold across persistent genuine and impostor identities. Count who changes from accepted to rejected instead of memorizing two density shapes.
figures.prediction: Which genuine speaker is rejected when the threshold rises to one?

individualReview.observation: The same ten genuine/impostor score identities stay fixed as the threshold rises zero-to-one, rejecting the remaining impostor and two formerly accepted genuine speakers.

figures.title: Only nonzero dual weights contribute to the SVM decision sum
figures.authoredReview: Keep all four training examples present, but stop routes whose dual weights are exactly zero.
figures.prediction: Does a zero dual contribution delete the corresponding training observation?

individualReview.observation: All four observations remain, but only .7/.4 nonzero dual weights have live sum routes; zero contributions from two/four are not missing or deleted examples.

figures.title: Learn the merge order from the corpus, then reuse it on new words
figures.authoredReview: The new word obeys a previously learned ordering. Retain character identity while consuming the three fixed merge instructions.
figures.prediction: Does encoding lower relearn pair priorities from that single word?

individualReview.observation: The new word lower consumes the fixed l-plus-o, lo-plus-w, and e-plus-r instructions in learned priority order; the retained character identities do not relearn a table from this word.

figures.title: Attention mixes token positions; the feed-forward layer transforms each position independently
figures.authoredReview: Rotate the connectivity emphasis without changing the token-feature grid. Attention connects token rows; feed-forward transformations connect features inside one row.
figures.prediction: Can one feed-forward application exchange information between different token rows?

individualReview.observation: The same token-feature grid highlights routes between token rows for attention and routes confined to each row for the feed-forward transformation; within-row mixing cannot exchange tokens.

figures.title: Changed gaps on the page do not establish changed high-dimensional distances
figures.authoredReview: Preserve each close pair while expanding the displayed gap between pairs. The drawing’s global separation should visibly change without altering the chosen local neighbors.
figures.prediction: Does the changed page gap establish a changed original-space distance?

individualReview.observation: The A/B and C/D close pairs remain intact in both views while the displayed between-group gap expands; the changed page geometry does not establish a changed original-space distance.

figures.title: An explicit approximation inside the band proves existence here, not trainability or generalization
figures.authoredReview: Show the actual approximating segments and separately magnify their error. Existence of this fit must not be mistaken for successful training or generalization.
figures.prediction: Does constructing these four segments prove a training algorithm will find them?

individualReview.observation: Four explicit piecewise-linear segments approximate the drawn square curve with maximum error one-sixty-fourth, below .02; the figure establishes existence in this family rather than successful training.

figures.title: Values need an action-selection rule; that rule can still be stochastic
figures.authoredReview: Keep equal action values fixed while two declared selection rules produce different actions or distributions.
figures.prediction: Which rule breaks the tie, and which rule preserves equal probability?

individualReview.observation: Equal-valued actions give equal .5/.5 softmax shares, whereas the declared greedy tie rule gives one/zero; the same values do not uniquely specify an action distribution.

figures.title: Four image patches become five tokens after adding the class token
figures.authoredReview: Carry four spatial patch identities into sequence positions, then prepend a visibly additional class token.
figures.prediction: Why does a two-by-two patch grid produce five sequence positions here?

individualReview.observation: Four separate image patches become four patch tokens plus one CLS token, giving five positioned sequence entries; the added summary position is not a fifth source patch.

figures.title: Adam rescales coupled L2 through its moments; AdamW applies decay directly
figures.authoredReview: Follow the coupled route through distinct frozen scales and the direct route around them. Equal weights alone do not equalize coupled shrinkage.
figures.prediction: Which route changes if the preconditioner grows from one to ten?

individualReview.observation: The blue coupled penalty passes through the illustrated adaptive path while the green .001 shrinkage bypasses it; equal nominal coefficients do not make their parameter updates identical.

figures.title: Masks share weights; prediction variation alone is not calibrated uncertainty
figures.authoredReview: Keep parameter identities fixed under both masks. Masked paths close without creating independently trained copies.
figures.prediction: Does the second mask introduce another independently trained w3?

individualReview.observation: Both masks retain the same w1/w2/w3 identities while changing live routes; inactive weights are not deleted and the two subnetworks are not separately trained parameter copies.

figures.title: Vector arithmetic creates a point; nearest-neighbor search selects a vocabulary word
figures.authoredReview: Move the same displacement arrow to a new origin. Its endpoint is a query coordinate before vocabulary search chooses an actual word.
figures.prediction: Does reaching coordinate (3,1) itself identify a vocabulary word?

individualReview.observation: Direct replacement inspection shows query above the arriving green arrow; translating the same one/one displacement gives coordinate three/one, with vocabulary lookup still a separate operation.

figures.title: Keep one conversation on one model to compare its outcome
figures.authoredReview: One outcome encloses all three turns. Contrast one conserved conversation assignment with an A-B-A sequence that contaminates the same outcome.
figures.prediction: Can this one conversation’s outcome isolate A after its middle turn uses B?

individualReview.observation: Three turns are bracketed into one outcome in both panels; the A/B/A middle-turn change visibly contaminates the conversation-level comparison.

figures.title: Sum locally, combine the partials, return 10 to every rank
figures.authoredReview: Keep the rank inputs separate until local grouping. Combine four and six once, then copy the completed ten into every rank destination.
figures.prediction: Does distributing the completed ten require adding it again?

individualReview.observation: The local pairs produce four and six, then one global ten is copied to all four ranks; distribution does not add the total again.

figures.title: Ordinary tests pass while protected records reveal a launch blocker
figures.authoredReview: A protected record has its own required route. Ordinary success cannot turn its failed record-rule gate into a pass.
figures.prediction: Does ordinary-case success authorize the protected-case violation?

individualReview.observation: The protected case reaches the failed record gate after passing speed, so the lower route stops instead of borrowing the ordinary-case pass.

figures.title: A passing agent test still misses the exact-expiry failure
figures.authoredReview: Make equality a distinct occupied boundary. Reject the boundary point as well as the expired region; only the strictly positive side passes.
figures.prediction: Which result follows when expiry minus now equals zero?

individualReview.observation: The equality point is red alongside expired time, and only strictly future expiry is green; the exact-boundary counterexample is visible on one ruler.

figures.title: Reduce each chunk on the ring, then circulate its completed sum
figures.authoredReview: Distinguish a growing partial from circulating completed data. The second route copies ten rather than summing four tens.
figures.prediction: After reduction reaches ten, should all-gather change its value?

individualReview.observation: The top partial progresses 1/3/6/10 through additions, while the bottom completed chunk stays ten at every forwarding point.

figures.title: A suppressed box cannot suppress its neighbours
figures.authoredReview: Retain the overlapping three-box chain and make the removed B route visibly unable to suppress C.
figures.prediction: Does B’s overlap with C matter after A has already removed B?

individualReview.observation: Aligned equal-height boxes show the adjacent overlaps; A suppresses B, the B-to-C route is inactive, and C remains green under the stated threshold.

figures.title: The experiment can finish before creator feedback arrives
figures.authoredReview: Keep the short-run observation boundary between viewer response and delayed creator response. The latter remains outside the first readout.
figures.prediction: Which response has not yet been observed when short-run analysis closes?

individualReview.observation: Creator response lies after the shared readout boundary while allocation and viewer response precede it, preventing the short experiment from claiming that later outcome.

figures.title: Permission comes before dispatch; outcome evidence comes after execution
figures.authoredReview: Execution has an authorization boundary, and a claimed effect has a receipt boundary. Pass both only on the fully evidenced route.
figures.prediction: Can a proposed action dispatch before its exact authorization?

individualReview.observation: The missing-authority row stops before its dashed receipt segment, while the authorized row reaches a receipt; proposal and outcome evidence remain different stages.

figures.title: Unscanned partitions stay unreachable, however good the distance estimate
figures.authoredReview: Put the actual nearest member physically inside excluded C. Improving representations within A and B cannot open the absent scan route.
figures.prediction: Can more accurate PQ distances inside A and B expose the true neighbor in C?

individualReview.observation: Only A and B receive live scan arrows, and the actual neighbor remains inside unscanned C; representation accuracy cannot bridge the absent route.

figures.title: The same scale exposes different time budgets in these fictional roles
figures.authoredReview: Use one hundred shared units per fictional role so the activity mix changes while total time stays fixed.
figures.prediction: Does the lead example have more total time, or a different allocation?

individualReview.observation: All three fictional role bars use the same hundred-unit width, revealing different research/build/coordination allocations without a benchmark claim.

figures.title: RNN-T can emit another token without advancing the audio frame
figures.authoredReview: Keep the time coordinate visibly fixed across a token edge, then move it only across the blank edge.
figures.prediction: Which edge changes audio time rather than output position?

individualReview.observation: A horizontal token transition preserves audio time and a vertical blank transition changes it; the two axes and their text explanations are not conflated.

figures.title: Append one new position or revise the whole provisional sample
figures.authoredReview: Retain committed prefix identities only on the autoregressive lane. Mark every diffusion position provisional until the completed sample.
figures.prediction: Can the middle diffusion sample be treated as a committed left prefix?

individualReview.observation: Reinspection shows both panel headings clear of the first circles; the upper prefix grows while every intermediate lower position remains provisional.

figures.title: A correct suggestion for an old document must still be discarded
figures.authoredReview: Carry the v7 request identity through the intervening v8 edit. The fast v7 reply must stop at the version-match gate.
figures.prediction: Does arriving quickly make the v7 answer applicable to v8?

individualReview.observation: The request and reply retain version seven around the intervening version-eight edit, so a correct old reply still cannot be applied without revalidation.

figures.title: Less alarming reasoning is not evidence of safer behaviour
figures.authoredReview: Change the explanation rail while preserving the prohibited action rail. A calmer text appearance does not alter the committed write.
figures.prediction: Which rail actually records whether the prohibited write changed?

individualReview.observation: Only the explanation rail changes from alarm to calm; the prohibited-write rail persists unchanged, preventing a calm explanation from becoming behavioral evidence.

figures.title: Keep the intermediate on chip to avoid its write-and-read trip
figures.authoredReview: The intermediate should follow an actual out-and-back HBM route in the unfused case, then stay on chip in the fitting fused case. Inputs and outputs still cross the boundary.
figures.prediction: Which traffic remains after the intermediate round trip disappears?

individualReview.observation: The unfused intermediate crosses the SRAM/HBM boundary twice, while the fitting fused intermediate stays on-chip and explicitly leaves input/output traffic intact.

figures.title: Two passing metrics cannot overrule the failed latency limit
figures.authoredReview: The launch rule is conjunction, not voting. Pass completion and cost, then stop the same release token at the latency gate.
figures.prediction: Can two passing gates compensate for latency 2.1 above its limit two?

individualReview.observation: Gain and cost pass before the red latency gate, and the displayed 2.1 limit breach blocks release instead of being outvoted by two green results.

figures.title: Look up the missing value, then return its saved earlier index
figures.authoredReview: The current value queries an earlier identity before inserting itself. Preserve the distinct saved index rather than matching a freshly stored current index.
figures.prediction: Which two original indices are returned when saved value two meets current value four?

individualReview.observation: The current four queries an earlier two before insertion; the saved value belongs to index one and the returned indices remain distinct.

figures.title: Score 0.62 means review only under the declared policy P7
figures.authoredReview: Place the score inside the explicitly versioned P7 action region. The score is a coordinate, not an intrinsic publishing permission.
figures.prediction: Which P7 region contains 0.62?

individualReview.observation: Score 0.62 sits inside the visibly bounded P7 review region, not an intrinsic allow/block interpretation independent of the declared policy.

figures.title: Four more accuracy points came with twice the compute
figures.authoredReview: Arrange task accuracy and compute on separate axes. Keep the missing baseline-at-two-times-compute cell open rather than attributing the full reported gain.
figures.prediction: Which missing result would isolate benefit at the new method’s resource budget?

individualReview.observation: The new two-times-compute result is separated from the one-times baseline, and the matched two-times baseline remains an explicit question mark.

figures.title: Choose splits that preserve users, time, and the evaluation claim
figures.authoredReview: Move the cut so all three identities of one user stay on one side. Contrast a random row assignment that divides the same user across train and test.
figures.prediction: Which assignment keeps user A from appearing on both sides?

individualReview.observation: Random row assignment puts the same A on both sides, while the group split keeps all three A identities together; the caption distinguishes group from time protections.

figures.title: A border point joins the cluster but cannot expand it
figures.authoredReview: Show E joining D’s neighborhood without acquiring D’s expansion authority. F remains disconnected; counts explicitly include self.
figures.prediction: Can border E expand the cluster when its neighborhood count is only two?

individualReview.observation: D's core neighborhood reaches border E, but E's dashed route cannot extend to F; membership and expansion authority are visibly different.

figures.title: Find the first failing rank and step before searching for its cause
figures.authoredReview: Traverse actual rank-time cells. Pin the first nonfinite cell at rank one, step two before showing the later shared symptoms.
figures.prediction: Do the three bad cells at step three identify where failure began?

individualReview.observation: The rank-one, step-two cell is singled out before the later step-three failures across ranks; row and column identities make the first failure specific.

figures.title: Fix the tiny-batch training path before tuning full-data generalization
figures.authoredReview: A nonzero gradient is not an applied update. Stop the route before delta weights and preserve the unchanged loss readout.
figures.prediction: Which observation distinguishes gradient computation from a real parameter step?

individualReview.observation: A nonzero .8 gradient has a broken route to zero weight change, leaving the tiny-batch loss flat rather than implying a completed optimizer step.

figures.title: Count fallback users before deciding which assigned treatment wins
figures.authoredReview: Intention-to-treat preserves the full assigned group. Circle the forty fallback identities as changed delivery, not removal from the experimental denominator.
figures.prediction: Does excluding fallback users preserve the originally assigned estimand?

individualReview.observation: Sixty exposed cases remain inside their original hundred-member cohort, and forty unexposed identities stay visible instead of being excluded or labeled negative.

figures.title: Clearing gradients and restoring training mode are separate operations
figures.authoredReview: Model mode and gradient buffer are independent persistent state. Let each action change only its own rail.
figures.prediction: After zeroing gradients in evaluation mode, which state still needs repair?

individualReview.observation: eval, zero, and train change only their own model-mode or gradient-buffer rail; the final state requires both training mode and a clean buffer.

figures.title: Choosing A gives up the higher assumed value of B plus C
figures.authoredReview: Put two feasible fixed-capacity portfolios side by side. Compatible B and C share the alternative whole, not two unrelated opportunities added without permission.
figures.prediction: Does past effort on A change its forward value eight versus eleven?

individualReview.observation: Two complete feasible portfolio bars compare assumed values eight versus eleven; past effort on A is explicitly outside the forward-value comparison.

figures.title: The second split affects only the root's right-hand region
figures.authoredReview: Draw the root boundary across the whole feature plane and the second cut only on its right branch.
figures.prediction: Does changing y above one move any x<=0 point out of A?

individualReview.observation: The horizontal second cut ends at the right-hand branch boundary, so every left-region point remains inside A regardless of its y coordinate.

figures.title: Judge the original decision using only evidence available at that time
figures.authoredReview: The committed decision boundary separates original evidence from later luck. Outcome observation cannot travel back into the decision-time evidence set.
figures.prediction: Was the later unexpected outcome available to the original decision maker?

individualReview.observation: The available-evidence point precedes the original decision boundary, while the later outcome lies after it and cannot certify the earlier process.

figures.title: Pending, censored, and unobserved outcomes are not negative labels
figures.authoredReview: Mature positives and negatives provide actual label routes. Pending and censored records stop before the label bucket without becoming zeros.
figures.prediction: Does a censored record belong in the observed negative bucket?

individualReview.observation: Mature positive and negative routes reach actual one/zero labels; pending and censored cases stop before unknown tokens instead of becoming negatives.

figures.title: The matched-control gap is 0.2 points, not the three-point headline
figures.authoredReview: Make the original-to-matched resource gain distinct from the small matched-to-method gap. Only the latter isolates the component under this setup.
figures.prediction: Which gap is the matched component effect: three or 0.2 points?

individualReview.observation: The eighty, 82.8, and eighty-three markers share the same ruler, making the matched-control .2 gap distinct from the headline three-point gain.

figures.title: Shared context does not grant every mode permission to execute tools
figures.authoredReview: Shared repository context reaches all four modes. Execution routes close in three modes and open only for a scoped isolated agent.
figures.prediction: Does having the same repository context grant chat execution authority?

individualReview.observation: All modes retain repository-context access, but only the agent row has a live authorized tool route; shared context does not silently grant execution authority.

figures.title: Persist authority before dispatch; reconcile a lost reply instead of paying twice
figures.authoredReview: The same idempotency identity must return one committed receipt after reply loss. Keep the account effect visibly singular across both requests.
figures.prediction: Does a lost response authorize creating a second payment?

individualReview.observation: The lost-reply reconciliation reuses key K and the original R1 receipt, preserving one account effect rather than creating a second payment.

figures.title: Restarted workers must agree on model, optimizer, and data state
figures.authoredReview: A recovery bundle needs all versions aligned. Trace the second rank’s matching weights through a stale optimizer gate.
figures.prediction: Can correct v4 weights repair the stale v3 optimizer state?

individualReview.observation: The lower rank's stale optimizer v3 breaks the otherwise matching model-v4/data-p8 bundle, so correct weights alone cannot permit restart.

figures.title: Use what was available then, not the latest value available now
figures.authoredReview: Draw B’s event and arrival on one clock around noon. Only A has crossed the availability boundary before the historical query.
figures.prediction: Can B’s earlier event time override its later 12:10 availability?

individualReview.observation: Version B has a pre-noon event but post-noon availability; the noon lookup admits available A, not the later version or its earlier event timestamp.

figures.title: Deleting a source does not erase its downstream model influence
figures.authoredReview: Source removal is only one known stage. Keep checkpoint and released-model influence as unresolved branches rather than completed deletion claims.
figures.prediction: Does excluding D7 from new data prove its old model influence was removed?

individualReview.observation: New-data exclusion has an observed result, while old-checkpoint and released-model influence remain explicit unknown stages requiring their own evidence.

figures.title: Declined and pending payments do not supply observed negative outcomes
figures.authoredReview: Policy affects whether an outcome can be observed. Keep approved outcomes, pending maturity, and declined missing outcomes on distinct routes.
figures.prediction: Can a declined payment be labeled legitimate from an unobserved repayment?

individualReview.observation: Direct reinspection shows a mature-approval route to an intact 0/1 token; pending and declined payments retain question marks and do not supply observed negative outcomes.

figures.title: Blocking one reproduced attack leaves other paths untested
figures.authoredReview: One reproduced direct attack is now blocked. Preserve quoted and tool-output paths as separate untested evidence obligations.
figures.prediction: Which attack paths still lack an observed post-fix result?

individualReview.observation: Only the reproduced direct attack has an observed post-fix result; quoted-attack and tool-output stages remain unknown rather than borrowed passes.

figures.title: A positive effect can still be too small or unsafe to launch
figures.authoredReview: Show the two candidates stopped at different gates. Statistical evidence does not replace practical benefit or safety.
figures.prediction: Which failed requirement remains after the nonzero-effect check passes?

individualReview.observation: One nonzero candidate stops at practical value, while another reaches the failed safety gate; neither can use the effect-sign pass as full launch authority.

figures.title: Staleness can breach a contract before outcome labels mature
figures.authoredReview: Separate immediately known freshness failure from outcome labels that mature later. Unknown future quality is not a delay in detecting the current contract breach.
figures.prediction: Which failure is already knowable before quality outcomes mature?

individualReview.observation: Freshness failure is placed at the immediate contract boundary, before maturation wait and the later quality readout, keeping staleness separate from delayed accuracy evidence.

figures.title: A stale attempt cannot overwrite the first valid committed result
figures.authoredReview: A version gate grants ownership only to the matching attempt. Carry A’s accepted version into B’s stale comparison and keep A’s result untouched.
figures.prediction: Can B overwrite A while still expecting version zero?

individualReview.observation: A's matching expected-zero comparison commits version one; B still expects zero and its broken write route cannot overwrite the accepted owner.

figures.title: Task success cannot excuse unauthorized account access
figures.authoredReview: Keep task completion and authorization as separate gates on the same trial. Unauthorized success remains a failed trial.
figures.prediction: Can successful completion override missing account authority?

individualReview.observation: Both trials pass the task gate, but the unauthorized trial ends at a red authority gate rather than inheriting the authorized trial's outcome.

figures.title: Free iteration slots do not imply free persistent memory
figures.authoredReview: Draw the persistent twelve-page ownership inventory separately from the eight reusable work slots. A new iteration refreshes only the work rail.
figures.prediction: Do free work slots release the nine pages already reserved by A and B?

individualReview.observation: Nine persistent A/B pages remain reserved while eight D/P work slots refresh; the two differently shaped inventories prevent treating compute slots as free memory.

figures.title: Quarterly accelerator-hours are not nodes available at this instant
figures.authoredReview: Carry the same eight node identities across serving pressure. Reclaim the two offline nodes only after their checkpoint-and-pause boundary.
figures.prediction: Do quarterly accelerator hours create another free node in this instantaneous pool?

individualReview.observation: The same eight node identities change from six serving/two offline to eight serving, so instantaneous reclaim does not create a ninth node from quarterly hours.

figures.title: Treatment changes shared supply that can later reach control users
figures.authoredReview: Keep one shared creator reservoir between the assigned cells. Changed supply returns to both future treatment and future control.
figures.prediction: Which return route breaks a simple no-interference interpretation?
